title: Azure Local infrastructure.yml
description: The one environment file for an Azure Local instance: the design choices, the machines, the networks, identity, Azure targets, provisioning (ISO or simplified machine provisioning with ZTP) and the cluster deployment. Every Azure Local tool reads this file: azurelocal-toolkit, azurelocal-ztp, Trailwright (writes it), Beacon, Sonar and Ranger. Keys are snake_case. Secrets are never values: they are keyvault://<vault>/<secret> references. Sections reject unknown keys; put anything else under extensions.

schema_version.description: The schema version this file follows. Major 5. A minor version adds optional keys only; a major version can rename or remove keys. Each key's description says which version added it ('since'). Version history, in order: 5.2 adds nodes[].network_adapters, BIOS settings, the site IP range and the maintenance environment's network. 5.3 adds the BIOS phases (bios_during_provisioning), networking.management.static_method and provisioning_dhcp_range, nodes[].maintenance_address, provisioning.simplified.maintenance_password, and the SAN details (storage.san.array, fibre_channel and iscsi, nodes[].san); it also adds _metadata.scope: ztp for a file that holds only what azurelocal-ztp reads. 5.4 puts every azurelocal-ztp setting in this schema, so no tool keeps a key of its own: the BIOS actions ZTP derives from the hardware inventory (provisioning.simplified.isolate_san_adapters and enable_embedded_nics, nodes[].san.hbas[].type), the Azure resource choices, timeouts, retries, the USB image and the maintenance environment of simplified provisioning, and hardware.bmc.rfs_write_attribute and verify_certificate. 5.4.1 adds provisioning.simplified.timeouts.adapters_minutes. 5.4.2 adds hardware.sbe.delivery and node_pull_url (how the SBE package reaches the nodes during OS configuration). 5.4.3 adds os_configuration.clear_storage, the switch that lets the OS configuration run wipe leftover local storage. 5.4.4 adds os_configuration.network (confirm_minutes, stable_seconds: the commit-confirmed window of a guarded network change) and os_configuration.remoting with transport, bootstrap_transport and allowed_source_cidrs. 5.5 puts the CI/CD infrastructure in devops (the project, its settings, the environments, the Azure sign-in, the runners with their network and roles) and adds the domain join (identity.active_directory.domain_join_account, join_options, local_admin_members). 5.6 adds the deployment block (the timeouts, polling, approval and resume of the toolkit's Validate and Deploy run) and the remote management security profile: scenario.environment_class, the profile keys of os_configuration.remoting (allow_any_source, trusted_hosts, use_https, isolation_confirmed, certificate; bootstrap_transport also takes smb and auto) and a purpose marker on networking.logical_networks[] and networking.cluster_networks[] (the values management and oob of networking.vlans[].purpose also count). A missing scenario.environment_class means production. 5.6.1 adds identity.active_directory.security_groups[].local_groups. 5.6.2 identifies the adapters of nodes[].network_adapters[] by hardware facts (mac_address is required; port_index, pci_location, vendor, os_name_override and allowed_vlans are optional). 5.6.3 adds enabled, ip_allocation_method and nsg_name to networking.logical_networks[]. A file written for 5.6.0 stays valid: a minor version adds optional keys only, except that 5.6.2 requires the MAC of every adapter. 5.6.4 adds the SBE package as a requirement: hardware.sbe.requirement and not_applicable_reason (whether the OEM package is required, or not applicable with a reason), source_path (the share or folder where the downloaded package is available to the automation), source_username and source_password (the read credential, a Key Vault reference), and the optional package_sha256 and package_size_bytes. The build-time side-load (delivery) is unchanged and stays off by default. 5.6.5 adds landing_zone.policy (required_tags, management_group): the tag names and the management group of the Tier 1 tag policy, which the Azure Policy task assigns in audit mode. 5.6.6 adds operations.monitoring.action_group: the name of the Azure Monitor action group that the alerting task creates. 5.6.7 adds security.defender_for_cloud: the free level of Microsoft Defender for Cloud that Azure Local needs. 5.6.8 adds security.defender_for_cloud.security_contact_email. 5.6.9 adds the storage keys the volume and storage path scripts read: storage.pool, storage.csv, storage.paths and, on storage.volumes, provisioning_type, file_system, parity_percent, media_type and deduplication. 5.6.10 adds what the SAN deployment needs: networking.cluster_network_properties and, for iSCSI, storage.san.iscsi.networks, jumbo_packet and chap.mutual. 5.6.11 adds what the logical network, network security group and VM image scripts read: networking.network_security_groups (name and rules with name, priority, direction, access, protocol, source and destination address prefixes and port ranges, description), networking.logical_networks[].vm_switch_name and storage.vm_images (name, os_type, publisher, offer, sku, version, storage_path). 5.6.12 adds operations.monitoring.retention_days and removes operations.notifications.teams_webhook and operations.monitoring.health_alerts. 5.6.13 adds the secrets section (provider, file directory, command) and lets a secret reference use the env://, file:// and command:// forms besides keyvault://. 5.6.14 adds hardware.inventory (output_directory, file_name_prefix, format, timeout_seconds), which Get-HardwareInventory.ps1 reads. 5.6.15 adds what Enable-ArcSdn.ps1 reads: sdn.acknowledge_maintenance_window and sdn.acknowledge_dns_record, the rules of sdn.prefix, and sdn.dns_records (read now); it removes sdn.default_access_policy. 5.6.16 adds storage.san.luns[].unique_id (how New-SanVolume.ps1 finds the disk of a LUN) and removes security.backup_key_vault. 5.6.17 adds landing_zone.management_groups[].role and azure.automation_identity.object_id (the two keys the Terraform landing zone and identity modules need) and makes the Terraform and Ansible code readers of the file (New-IacVariableFiles.ps1). 5.6.19 adds provisioning.iso.image_uri (the address Invoke-MountGoldImageISO.ps1 gives the BMC virtual media), landing_zone.subscriptions[].billing_scope and workload, point_to_site.protocols, root_certificate_name and root_certificate, bastion.network and the nat_gateway object of landing_zone.connectivity, and a list of values for landing_zone.virtual_machines[].os. 5.6.20 adds operations.updates.install_after_deployment and operations.updates.target_version (read by Start-SolutionUpdateAfterDeployment.ps1) and removes keys that no tool read (see MIGRATION, To 5.6.20). 5.6.21 adds landing_zone.network_security_groups[] (the network security groups of the Azure landing zone networks: name and rules, created by New-LandingZoneNsg.ps1) and security.baseline_settings[] (type, name, value and acknowledge_weaker_security of the security baseline settings that Set-SecurityBaselines.ps1 changes with Set-AzsSecurity). The current version is 5.6.21.

scope.description: Schema 5.3. full (default): the whole instance, so every design section is required (scenario, environment, cluster, networking.intents, identity and the sections a scenario choice makes required). ztp: a file for azurelocal-ztp on its own, with no automation after it. It holds only what ZTP reads, so the cluster deployment's sections (cluster, intents, storage, identity beyond local_admin) are not required. Use infrastructure.ztp.example.yml to start one. To grow it into the full file, add the rest and set scope to full (or remove the key).

file_version.description: Your own version of this file.

last_updated.description: Date of the last change, YYYY-MM-DD.

generated_by.description: The tool that wrote the file, for example azurelocal-trailwright 1.1.0. Empty when written by hand.

notes.description: Free text about this file for the people who keep it. Not read by the tools.

scenario.description: The design choices. Every other section is read in the light of these: a choice makes its section required, and tools pick their path from here. All of them are required, so nothing is assumed.

identity.description: active_directory: machines join an AD domain (needs identity.active_directory). local_identity: no AD, secrets in Key Vault (needs identity.local_identity). https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/deploy/deployment-local-identity-with-key-vault

storage_architecture.description: s2d: Storage Spaces Direct (hyperconverged). san: external SAN only (disaggregated; needs storage.san). hybrid: both (S2D plus a SAN). san and hybrid TELL THE SOLUTION THERE IS A SAN: the OS configuration then does the host-side SAN work itself (the Mpio step: MPIO, MSDSM hardware ID, the MPIO claim of the device (mpclaim -n -i -d), load balance policy, vendor MPIO settings; for iSCSI the initiator service, auto-claim, portals and sessions, except for a san design on Azure Local 2610 or later, where the deployment configures iSCSI and Microsoft Learn says not to enable it before) and checks each LUN is seen once (SanVerify). storage.san.type says whether the SAN is fibre_channel or iscsi. On every node the OS configuration also looks, read only, for FC or iSCSI LUNs that are visible while the file declares no SAN, and reports them. https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/deploy/enable-external-storage

storage_connectivity.description: switched: storage traffic goes through top-of-rack switches. switchless: machines are cabled directly to each other for storage. A single machine uses switched.

topology.description: standard, or rack_aware (machines split across two local availability zones; every node needs a zone).

connectivity.description: connected to Azure, or disconnected operations (needs the disconnected section).

cloud.description: Azure public cloud or Azure Government.

outbound_path.description: How the machines reach Azure. Paths with a proxy need networking.outbound.proxy; paths with Arc gateway need networking.outbound.arc_gateway; private_path needs networking.outbound.private_path.

os_install.description: iso: the OS is installed from an ISO (by hand or out-of-band). simplified: simplified machine provisioning from Azure, which azurelocal-ztp automates (needs provisioning.simplified, and on every node a serial number, a BMC address and the management MAC: management.mac_address, or from 5.2 a mac_address on every network_adapters port with role management and at least one port with role provisioning).

deploy_method.description: How the cluster is deployed: the Azure portal or an ARM template. Documentation only; not read by the tools. The toolkit deploys with the ARM template; no tool branches on this key.

environment_class.description: What kind of environment this is. It picks the remote management security profile of the OS configuration run (WinRM, RDP and ICMP scope on the nodes, HTTP or HTTPS, the TrustedHosts policy of the machine running the automation, the one-time Arc bootstrap): see docs/os-configuration-and-arm-deployment.md and config/remoting-profiles.json. lab and test are relaxed with the wildcard (TrustedHosts '*', sources Any, HTTP 5985 allowed) and a warning says so; dev, production and dmz are strict. Optional. Missing means production (fail closed); another value is rejected. (since 5.6)

customer.description: Name of the customer or organization the site belongs to. Documentation only; not read by the tools.

time_zone.description: Windows time zone ID of the site, for example UTC or Eastern Standard Time. Simplified provisioning sets it on the site. The OS configuration's Time step sets it on every node (Set-TimeZone, only when it differs) and leaves the zone alone when the key is empty. Learn: the Configurator app sets the time zone with the time server.

code.description: Short site code, 2 to 8 uppercase letters or digits.

location.description: Physical location, for example a city.

datacenter.description: Short code or name of the datacenter or room that holds the machines. Documentation only; not read by the tools.

name.description: Display name of the site. Also the display name of the Microsoft.Edge site in simplified provisioning.

owner.description: Contact (a team mailbox, not a person) who owns the site. Documentation only; not read by the tools.

name.description: Environment identifier: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Documentation only; not read by the tools. It repeats site.name for the tools; Trailwright writes it.

type.description: Class of the environment: lab, demo, poc, dev, test, stg or prd. Documentation only; not read by the tools: scenario.environment_class is the key that changes what the tools allow.

owner.description: Contact (a team mailbox) that owns the environment. Documentation only; not read by the tools.

description.description: One sentence on what the environment is for. Documentation only; not read by the tools.

tags.description: Azure tags applied to the resources the tools create. A policy that requires tags isn't supported by simplified provisioning.

azure.description: The Azure targets of the instance: tenant, region, and the subscription and resource group of the Arc machines, the cluster and (unless provisioning.simplified says otherwise) the site and edge machines.

tenant_id.description: Microsoft Entra tenant ID (GUID) of the subscription. Read it with (Get-AzContext).Tenant.Id or from the Microsoft Entra ID overview page in the Azure portal.

location.description: Azure region, for example eastus. Simplified provisioning works only in eastus in the preview.

subscription_id.description: Subscription ID (GUID) of the Arc machines and the cluster, and of the site and edge machines unless provisioning.simplified.subscription_id names another one. Read it with (Get-AzContext).Subscription.Id.

resource_group.description: Resource group of the Arc machines and the cluster: 1 to 90 characters (letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, period, parentheses). The Azure Local resource provider needs the Azure Connected Machine Resource Manager role on it; the ZTP template assigns that role.

hci_resource_provider_object_id.description: Object ID of the Azure Local resource provider's service principal (application 1412d89f-b8a8-4111-b4fd-e82905cbd85d) in the tenant. Optional: tools look it up when they can read the directory.

custom_location.description: Name of the custom location the deployment creates.

automation_identity.description: The identity that runs automation with no one signed in (pipelines, ZTP, the ARM deployment).

type.description: The kind of identity that runs the automation: a managed identity (preferred, no secret to keep) or a service principal.

name.description: Managed identity resource name, or the service principal's display name.

client_id.description: Client (application) ID of the identity (GUID). Not a secret.

object_id.description: Object ID (GUID) of the identity's principal in Microsoft Entra ID. Not a secret. The Terraform identity module assigns the roles of the deployment identity to this ID. Read it from the identity in the Azure portal, or with Get-AzADServicePrincipal.

resource_group.description: Resource group that holds the identity.

key_vaults.description: Every Key Vault that a keyvault:// reference in this file names, with where it is. Tools resolve references against this list, and grant roles on the vault from it.

name.description: Key Vault name, as a keyvault://<name>/<secret> reference uses it: 3 to 24 characters, letters, digits and hyphens.

resource_group.description: Resource group that holds the vault.

purpose.description: What the vault holds, for example management, deployment or backup.

secrets.description: Schema 5.6.13. Where the toolkit reads secrets from. Every secret in this file is a reference, never a value; a reference names its own provider in its scheme: keyvault://<vault>/<secret> (Azure Key Vault, the default), env://<VARIABLE_NAME>, file://<name> or command://<name>. One file can mix providers. A file or command reference holds a NAME only: the directory of the secret files and the command are set here, so a reference in a shared file cannot point a machine at an arbitrary path or run an arbitrary command. Optional; every key has a default. See docs/secret-references.md.

provider.description: Schema 5.6.13. The provider New-AzlSecretReference uses for a new reference when the caller does not name one. It does not change how an existing reference is read: that follows the reference's own scheme. Default keyvault.

file.description: Schema 5.6.13. Settings of the file provider (file://<name>). Needed only when a reference uses it.

directory.description: Schema 5.6.13. The absolute path of the directory that holds the secret files. file://<name> reads the file <name> in it: one secret per file, UTF-8, the trailing line break removed. A name cannot hold a path, so no reference can leave this directory. Links are refused. A warning is written when Everyone, Users or Authenticated Users (Windows), or group or other (Linux, macOS), can read the file.

command.description: Schema 5.6.13. Settings of the command provider (command://<name>). Needed only when a reference uses it. The toolkit starts the executable directly with the argument list, with no shell, closes its standard input and reads its standard output as the secret (the trailing line break removed). A command that exits with a code other than 0 fails, and its standard error is reported without the secret.

executable.description: Schema 5.6.13. The program to start: a command name found on the path, or an absolute path. Not a command line: the arguments are in command.arguments.

arguments.description: Schema 5.6.13. The arguments, one list item each. The text {name} in an item is replaced by the name in the reference (command://<name>). At least one item must hold {name}. Each item is passed as one argument; nothing is split or quoted by a shell.

timeout_seconds.description: Schema 5.6.13. How long the command may run before it is stopped and the read fails. Default 30.

cluster.description: The Azure Local instance (the cluster deployment).

name.description: Cluster name: a NetBIOS name of up to 15 characters. ARM parameter clusterName.

naming_prefix.description: Prefix of the Azure resources the deployment creates. ARM parameter namingPrefix.

deployment_mode.description: ARM deploymentMode: validate runs the checks only; deploy deploys.

witness.description: The quorum witness of the cluster. A two-machine cluster and a rack aware cluster need one (rule AZL-008). See cluster.witness.type.

type.description: cloud (an Azure Storage account), file_share (disconnected operations), or none. Two machines need a witness. https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/concepts/cluster-witness

storage_account.description: Cloud witness storage account. ARM clusterWitnessStorageAccountName.

key_vault.description: The Key Vault the deployment uses for the instance's secrets (one per instance). ARM keyVaultName.

name.description: Name of the Key Vault the deployment creates for the cluster (ARM keyVaultName): 3 to 24 characters, letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter.

soft_delete_retention_days.description: Days a deleted secret or vault stays recoverable, 7 to 90.

diagnostics.description: Key Vault audit logs. ARM diagnosticStorageAccountName, logsRetentionInDays and storageAccountType.

storage_account.description: Name of the storage account that receives the cluster diagnostic logs: 3 to 24 lowercase letters and digits.

logs_retention_days.description: Days the diagnostic logs are kept.

storage_account_type.description: SKU of the diagnostic storage account, for example Standard_LRS.

deployment.description: How the toolkit's ARM Validate and Deploy run (Invoke-AzureLocalArmDeployment.ps1) waits, asks for approval and recovers. Optional; every key has a default; a -Settings value on the command line wins over this block. (since 5.6)

validate_timeout_minutes.description: How long the run waits for a Validate before it stops waiting (state ValidationTimedOut; Azure keeps working and the next run attaches to it). Microsoft: validation takes about 10 to 30 minutes. Default 90. (since 5.6)

deploy_timeout_minutes.description: How long the run waits for a Deploy before it stops waiting (state DeploymentTimedOut). Microsoft: 2.5 to 3 hours; several steps take 40 to 50 minutes or more. Default 360. (since 5.6)

poll_seconds.description: Seconds between the first reads of the validation or deployment status. The delay grows by half each read up to poll_max_seconds. Default 15. (since 5.6)

poll_max_seconds.description: The longest delay between two reads. Default 120. (since 5.6)

approval.description: Mode ValidateAndDeploy: what happens between a good Validate and the Deploy. stop (default): the run ends in state AwaitingApproval and a later run with Mode Deploy continues. prompt: asks on the console, and stops without a console. none: continues at once (a lab). Pipelines run Validate and Deploy as two jobs with the platform's approval between them and do not use this. (since 5.6)

resume.description: Allow the run to resubmit a failed Deploy (and attach to a running one). Without it a failed Deploy is refused. Microsoft's portal has Resume deployment for a failed instance; for the ARM route this resubmits the same parameters in Deploy mode. Default false. (since 5.6)

require_os_configuration_report.description: Fail the precondition OsConfigurationConverged when no OS configuration report is given, instead of skipping it with a warning. Default false. (since 5.6)

skip_preconditions.description: Preconditions to skip on purpose. They appear in the report as Skipped, never hidden. (since 5.6)

acknowledge_known_issues.description: Ids from config/known-issues/arm-deployment.json that you accept, so a precondition or a resume that a known issue would block goes ahead (for example arc-device-id-name). Leave empty normally. (since 5.6)

deployment_settings_api_version.description: Patch the deploymentSettings api-version in Microsoft's template (for example 2026-10-01) when the template's own preview version is retired. Default: the template's. (since 5.6)

solution_version.description: The solution version the nodes run (four numeric parts, for example 12.2610.1004.50). The precondition SbeValidatedWithSolution compares it with the solution versions the OEM's SBE discovery catalog lists for the configured SBE. Leave empty to use the ZTP handoff's solution version, else the version derived from the nodes' OS build (reported as derived; only builds that map unambiguously). The OS configuration also passes it to the Arc registration of a machine installed from an ISO as -TargetSolutionVersion, the version the first deployment uses; without it the registration cmdlet asks which version to use, which an unattended run cannot answer.

sbe_catalog_path.description: The OEM's SBE discovery catalog (SBE_Discovery_Dell.xml) the precondition SbeValidatedWithSolution reads: the file, or a folder that holds SBE_Discovery_*.xml. Default: the SBE_Discovery_*.xml in hardware.sbe.source_path, else hardware.sbe.bundle_path. Nothing is downloaded.

pre_cluster_verification_max_age_hours.description: How long a passing result of the pre-cluster verification gate (Invoke-AzureLocalPreClusterVerification.ps1 -Mode Verify) stays valid for the ARM Validate and Deploy, in hours. After that the ARM run fails the precondition PreClusterVerification and names the command to run again. Default 4. (since 5.6)

verification_min_memory_gib.description: Minimum memory per node in GiB for the pre-cluster verification (Learn: system requirements, at least 32 GB). Default 32. (since 5.6)

verification_min_boot_disk_gb.description: Minimum boot drive size in GB for the pre-cluster verification (Learn: at least 200 GB). Default 200. (since 5.6)

verification_min_data_disk_gb.description: Minimum size in GB of the data drives of a Storage Spaces Direct node for the pre-cluster verification (Learn: at least two drives of 500 GB). Default 500. (since 5.6)

verification_min_link_gbps.description: Minimum link speed in Gbps of the storage adapters for the pre-cluster verification (Learn: at least 10 Gbps for RDMA or iSCSI storage traffic). Default 10. (since 5.6)

verification_max_clock_skew_seconds.description: Largest clock difference in seconds between a node and this host that the pre-cluster verification accepts (Kerberos allows 300). Default 300. (since 5.6)

pre_cluster_verification_report_director.description: Where the pre-cluster verification gate writes report.json, summary.md and precluster-verification-events.jsonl, and where the ARM run looks for the latest result. Default: arm-report\verification\live in the environment data folder (the folder that holds provisioning.simplified.evidence_path, else media_path, else the folder of the infrastructure file). (since 5.6)

register_resource_providers.description: Opt in to registering the mandatory Azure Local resource providers (Microsoft Learn: Assign required permissions for Azure Local deployment) that are not registered in the subscription, and waiting until they are Registered, when the precondition ResourceProviders runs in Mode Validate or Deploy. Default false: the run never changes Azure by itself and a mandatory provider that is not registered fails the precondition, with the Register-AzResourceProvider command for each. Needs Owner or Contributor on the subscription. Never done in Plan or with WhatIf. Set by the -RegisterResourceProviders switch. (since 5.6)

nodes.description: The machines, one entry each. ARM physicalNodesSettings and arcNodeResourceIds. Up to 16 with Storage Spaces Direct, up to 64 disaggregated (the validator checks which applies).

name.description: Host name: up to 15 characters. Also the edge machine name and, for an ISO install, the Arc machine name. With simplified provisioning the Arc machine name is arc_machine_name, which defaults to this.

management.description: The machine's management port and address (schema 5.0 and 5.1). From 5.2, network_adapters describes it instead: the port with role management and an ip_assignment other than none. When both are given they must agree; prefer network_adapters.

ip_address.description: Management address. ARM physicalNodesSettings[].ipv4Address. How it gets onto the management port before deployment is networking.management.ip_assignment: set on the port (static), reserved in DHCP for mac_address (dhcp), or already there (preconfigured). With network_adapters it is the management port's ip_address.

mac_address.description: MAC of the management port. Provisioning finds and targets the port by it: simplified provisioning names the port by this MAC when it sets the static address (edge machine networkAdapters[].macAddress), and node preparation finds the adapter by it. With ip_assignment dhcp, reserve ip_address for this MAC. Required with simplified provisioning.

adapter_name.description: Name of the management port in the installed OS, for example 'SLOT 3 Port 1'. Optional: mac_address identifies the port. Simplified provisioning also sends it with the port's settings; leave it out unless you know the name the OS gives the port.

network_adapters.description: Every physical network port of the machine (schema 5.2): name, MAC, roles and how each gets its host address. Exactly one port owns the management address: role management and an ip_assignment other than none. Intents name ports by these names. List them on every node or on none.

name.description: The port's name in this file: the key that networking.intents[].adapters, networking.storage.networks[].adapter and networking.cluster_networks[].adapter use. The same on every machine, unique on the machine. It labels a physical adapter that is found on the node by mac_address, so it does not have to be the name the OS gave the adapter (OS names differ between installs and between ZTP and ISO installs, for example Port0, SLOT 3 Port 1 or NIC1). Discovery writes it from the slot and the port, for example 'Slot 3 Port 1'. The name the deployment sends to Azure is what the OS calls the adapter (read by MAC) or os_name_override when set. A file that already uses the OS name here keeps working.

mac_address.description: The port's identity. Tools find the physical adapter on a node by this MAC (case and separators are ignored), never by a name: node preparation, the ARM parameters and the pre-cluster verification all resolve the OS adapter name from it. Hardware discovery writes it. Required. Also needed for a DHCP reservation and, with simplified provisioning, for the management port.

slot.description: Where the port is, for example Embedded (a LOM), Slot 3 or OCP 1. From 5.4 azurelocal-ztp reads it: a management or provisioning port in slot Embedded makes it enable the embedded NICs in the BIOS (provisioning.simplified.enable_embedded_nics), and a slot that also holds a SAN adapter (nodes[].san.hbas[].slot) is never turned off.

port_index.description: The number of the port on its adapter, counted from 1, as the BMC reports it (Redfish PhysicalPortNumber, else the order of the port on the card). With slot and pci_location it says which physical connector the port is. Written by hardware discovery; a record of the hardware, nothing is configured from it. Documentation only; not read by the tools.

pci_location.description: Where the adapter sits on the PCI bus, as hardware discovery reports it (bus, device, function as decimal numbers). A verification aid, informational: OS configuration compares it with the node's own hardware information (Get-NetAdapterHardwareInfo) and reports a difference; the port is still found by mac_address.

vendor.description: The adapter manufacturer as hardware discovery reports it, for example the Manufacturer of the Redfish NetworkAdapter. Informational: no tool behaves differently for a brand; every make is handled through the same keys (mac_address, slot, port_index, model, speed_gbps, rdma). Documentation only; not read by the tools.

os_name_override.description: Optional, off by default. The name you want this adapter to have in the OS, for example 'Mgmt1', 'Compute1' or 'Storage1'. Without it nothing is renamed: the OS configuration step NicNames leaves every adapter name alone and the deployment sends the name the OS already uses (found by mac_address). With it, NicNames renames the adapter found by mac_address to this name (a guarded change, idempotent, the management adapter last) and the deployment sends this name. Give the same value for the same port (name) on every machine: Network ATC needs one adapter name per intent adapter on every node. 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, space, underscore, dot, hyphen and parentheses.

model.description: Card model, for example 'NVIDIA ConnectX-6 Dx'. Ports in one intent must be the same make, model and speed.

speed_gbps.description: Link speed of the port in Gbit/s, as the BMC reports it.

rdma.description: RDMA technology the port supports: none, iwarp, roce (RoCE) or roce_v2 (RoCEv2). A record of the hardware; what is sent to Azure is networking.intents[].overrides.adapter.network_direct_technology. Documentation only; not read by the tools.

roles.description: What the port is for: management, compute, storage (the Network ATC traffic types), provisioning (the maintenance environment of simplified provisioning reaches Azure through this port, before the machine is claimed; how it gets its address there is networking.management.provisioning_network), iscsi:a or iscsi:b (schema 5.3: a port that carries iSCSI traffic to the SAN's fabric A or B; give it a static address, prefix_length and VLAN, no gateway), or unused. A converged port lists several, for example [management, compute]. unused stands alone.

ip_assignment.description: How the installed OS gets this port's host address before deployment. For the management port this is the management address mode (config/variables/docs/infrastructure-file.md): dhcp_reservation is Mode A (Reserved, recommended); static is Mode B (Static with DHCP) or Mode C (Static without management DHCP). static: ip_address is set on the port (with simplified provisioning azurelocal-ztp's Device stage sets it by MAC before the OS install, the install resets every port to DHCP, and OS configuration sets it again by MAC; otherwise the operator or the toolkit). dhcp_reservation: the port keeps DHCP and the DHCP server reserves ip_address for mac_address. dhcp: the port keeps DHCP with no reservation, so its address can change (a warning). preconfigured: the port is already configured; tools leave it alone. none: no host address before deployment (Network ATC or the storage networks give it one, or it isn't used); node preparation turns DHCP off on it. Exactly one management port per machine owns the management address: the one with role management and an ip_assignment other than none.

ip_address.description: The host address. For the management port this is ARM physicalNodesSettings[].ipv4Address. Required with static. With dhcp_reservation give the reserved address: without it the tools can only check that the port has a DHCP address (a warning), and the deployment still needs it unless use_dhcp is true (a file with scope ztp doesn't deploy).

prefix_length.description: Prefix length of ip_address. Default for the management port: from networking.management.subnet, which it must match.

gateway.description: Default gateway on this port. Default for the management port: networking.management.gateway. Leave it out on every other port: validation fails when more than one physical adapter has a default gateway.

dns_servers.description: Default for the management port: networking.management.dns_servers, which it must match.

vlan_id.description: The VLAN of this port's traffic. With vlan_mode tagged the host tags it; with vlan_mode access the switch port is an access port in this VLAN and the host sends untagged frames (it records the switch side). Without vlan_mode, 0 or absent means untagged and anything else is tagged by the host.

vlan_mode.description: access: the switch port is an access (untagged) port; the host doesn't tag, so simplified provisioning sends VLAN 0. tagged: the switch port is a trunk and the host tags vlan_id.

allowed_vlans.description: Optional. The VLAN ids the switch port of this adapter allows, when the port is a trunk that carries more than the VLAN of the port itself: the tenant (compute) VLANs of the compute adapters. The pre-cluster verification checks that every VLAN used by compute traffic in networking.vlans[] and networking.logical_networks[] is in this list on the compute adapters; without it a tagged compute port is reported Skipped (the file says nothing about what the port allows). This is switch-side metadata for the checklist of the gate; it does not configure the switch or the NIC.

switch.description: The switch, for example a network_devices[].hostname.

port.description: The switch port, for example Ethernet1/11.

description.description: Free text about the switch port, for example the cable label. Documentation only; not read by the tools. A label for the cabling record; the gate reads switch_port.switch and port only.

serial_number.description: Serial number (Dell service tag). Maps each simplified-provisioning voucher to its machine.

bmc.description: The baseboard management controller (BMC) of the machine: address, type and login. ZTP drives the machine through it over Redfish (virtual media, boot override, BIOS settings, power); hardware discovery reads the machine through it.

ip_address.description: IPv4 address of the BMC (iDRAC, iLO, XCC). It must answer HTTPS (TCP 443) from the host that runs ZTP or discovery.

type.description: Kind of BMC: idrac (Dell), ilo (HPE), xcc (Lenovo) or other. Only Dell iDRAC is proven end to end in this phase; BMC kinds other than idrac are planned. Hardware inventory (Get-HardwareInventory.ps1) compares it with the vendor it detects from the Redfish answers; other is not compared.

username.description: BMC account name. The plain name, or a keyvault:// reference.

password.description: A Key Vault secret reference: keyvault://<vault>/<secret>. The vault must be listed in key_vaults.

rack.description: Rack identifier, for the as-built record. Documentation only; not read by the tools. A location label; the deployment uses nodes[].zone.

rack_position.description: Position in the rack, for example U12, for the as-built record.

zone.description: Rack-aware: the local availability zone. ARM localAvailabilityZones.

storage_ips.description: Storage address on each storage network, in networking.storage.networks order, when networking.storage.auto_ip is false.

arc_machine_name.description: Name of the machine's Arc resource (Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines). Default: name. Simplified provisioning sets it when it claims the machine (edge machine arcMachineResourceId); without it the service names the Arc machine ROE1-<id>, and an Arc machine can't be renamed. The deployment uses it in ARM arcNodeResourceIds. An ISO install registers the Arc machine under the host name, so leave it out there. 1-54 letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.', not ending in '.'.

arc_resource_name.description: Deprecated: use arc_machine_name. Read as arc_machine_name when that isn't set.

bios.description: BIOS attributes for this machine in their FINAL state, merged over hardware.bios (a key here wins). See hardware.bios.

bios_during_provisioning.description: Schema 5.3. Temporary BIOS attributes for this machine's OS install only, merged over hardware.bios_during_provisioning (a key here wins); during-provisioning values win over bios. azurelocal-ztp sets each key back to its bios value in its Restore stage. See hardware.bios_during_provisioning.

maintenance_address.description: Schema 5.3. Simplified provisioning: the address the machine's maintenance environment answers on (its Configurator service, TCP 20001), when it is known: a DHCP reservation, or an address set at the console. azurelocal-ztp's Device stage then talks to it directly. Without it, the Device stage finds the maintenance environment by MAC, scanning networking.management.provisioning_dhcp_range.

san.description: Schema 5.3. This machine's SAN connections: its Fibre Channel HBAs and their WWPNs (storage.san.type fibre_channel), or its iSCSI initiator IQN (storage.san.type iscsi; the iSCSI ports' addresses are on network_adapters with role iscsi:a and iscsi:b). Needed on every machine when storage.san.type is set.

hbas.description: The host bus adapters in this machine that reach the SAN: Fibre Channel HBAs, and from 5.4 iSCSI offload adapters. azurelocal-ztp reads their slots (schema 5.4): while the OS installs it turns those PCIe slots off in the BIOS, so the maintenance environment can't install onto a SAN LUN, and turns them on again afterwards (provisioning.simplified.isolate_san_adapters).

slot.description: Where the HBA is, as a PCIe slot label: Slot 2, Slot2 or slot-2 (the number is what counts). azurelocal-ztp turns the BIOS attribute of that slot off for the OS install and puts it back afterwards; the attribute name per vendor is in its config/oem/<vendor>.json. For another label (for example OCP 1), or a vendor azurelocal-ztp has no mapping for, give bios_attribute.

type.description: Schema 5.4. fibre_channel (default; with storage.san.type fibre_channel the ports with their WWPNs are needed for zoning, rule AZL-028) or iscsi_offload (an adapter that presents SAN LUNs to the BIOS; it needs no ports here, its addresses are on network_adapters with role iscsi:a or iscsi:b).

bios_attribute.description: Schema 5.4. The vendor's BIOS attribute name for this adapter's slot, as the BMC's Redfish Bios resource names it. With no vendor mapping in azurelocal-ztp this is the only way to isolate the adapter during the install; with a mapping it overrides the attribute derived from slot. An explicit bios_during_provisioning key for the same attribute still wins.

bios_disabled_value.description: Schema 5.4. The value of bios_attribute that turns the slot off for the OS install. Default: the vendor mapping's disabled value, else Disabled.

bios_enabled_value.description: Schema 5.4. The value that turns the slot back on when azurelocal-ztp finds it already at bios_disabled_value in the Restore stage (for example a crashed earlier run left it off). Otherwise Restore puts back the value it found before the install. Default: the vendor mapping's enabled value, else Enabled.

model.description: Model of the host bus adapter, as the machine reports it.

ports.description: The ports of the host bus adapter.

initiator_iqn.description: The machine's iSCSI initiator name. Unique in the file.

hardware.description: What every machine is. The layout is the same on every machine.

vendor.description: OEM, for example Dell, HPE, Lenovo or DataON. ZTP picks config/oem/<vendor>.json from it.

model.description: Model, for example AX-760. Used to select the SBE.

cpu_cores.description: Physical cores per machine. Get-HardwareInventory.ps1 compares it with the cores the BMC reports (the sum over all processors).

memory_gib.description: Memory per machine, GiB. Get-HardwareInventory.ps1 compares it with the memory the BMC reports.

gpu.description: GPUs fitted in every machine. Leave out when there are none. Get-HardwareInventory.ps1 compares these keys with the GPUs the BMC reports.

enabled.description: true when the machines carry GPUs.

model.description: GPU model, as the machine reports it.

count_per_node.description: Number of GPUs in each machine.

bmc.description: BMC (iDRAC, iLO, XCC) login used for every machine unless a node sets its own.

username.description: A reference to the secret holding the user name, or the user name itself.

password.description: A Key Vault secret reference: keyvault://<vault>/<secret>. The vault must be listed in key_vaults.

rfs_write_attribute.description: Schema 5.4. azurelocal-ztp, Boot stage: also set the iDRAC Remote File Share attribute RFS.<n>.WriteProtected to Read Write before it inserts the virtual media. iDRAC 7.30 rejects WriteProtected=false in InsertMedia, and the maintenance environment cannot write its voucher to a read-only drive. Default: true for Dell (azurelocal-ztp config/oem/dell.json, bmc.rfsWriteAttribute), false for the other vendors, whose BMCs have no such attribute. Set it when your BMC differs from its vendor's usual behaviour.

verify_certificate.description: Schema 5.4. Check the BMCs' TLS certificates. Default false: BMCs ship a self-signed certificate, so azurelocal-ztp accepts it. Set true once the BMCs carry a certificate that the management host trusts.

inventory.description: Schema 5.6.14. Where Get-HardwareInventory.ps1 writes the hardware inventory it reads from the BMCs, in which format, and how long it waits for a BMC. The script reads every BMC over the standard Redfish API (read only), for any maker, and writes one file per run. Leave the block out to use the defaults. The file holds serial numbers and MAC addresses: keep the folder out of git.

output_directory.description: Schema 5.6.14. The folder the inventory file is written to. It is created when it is missing. Default: hardware-inventory, relative to the folder the script runs from.

file_name_prefix.description: Schema 5.6.14. The start of the file name. The file is named <prefix>-<UTC time>.<json or yml>, so every run writes a new file and keeps the old ones. 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. Default: hardware-inventory.

format.description: Schema 5.6.14. The format of the inventory file: json or yaml. Default: json.

timeout_seconds.description: Schema 5.6.14. How long the script waits for one answer of a BMC, in seconds. A BMC is a small computer and can be slow. Default: 60.

bios.description: BIOS attributes for every machine, as they are when the machine is finished (schema 5.2; from 5.3 this is the FINAL state): a node's bios is merged over it. azurelocal-ztp applies them at its Boot stage, and in its Restore stage sets back to these values any key that bios_during_provisioning changed for the OS install. See $defs/bios_settings.

bios_during_provisioning.description: Schema 5.3. BIOS attributes that hold for the OS install only: TEMPORARY values. A node's bios_during_provisioning is merged over this one, and during-provisioning values win over bios. azurelocal-ztp applies them at its Boot stage. In its Restore stage, after the OS install and before Handoff, it sets each key back to its bios value (or, when bios doesn't name the key, to the original value it saved), restarts the node and waits for Arc to reconnect. From 5.4 azurelocal-ztp derives the SAN-adapter case itself from nodes[].san.hbas[].slot (provisioning.simplified.isolate_san_adapters); the raw keys remain as explicit overrides and win. Example: bios { Slot2: Enabled } with bios_during_provisioning { Slot2: Disabled } turns off a Fibre Channel HBA in slot 2 while the maintenance environment installs the OS (it would otherwise install onto the SAN LUN), and turns it on again afterwards. On Dell, a slot can also be BootDriverDisabled: visible to the OS but never a boot device. A key here should also be in bios, so the final state is explicit. See $defs/bios_settings.

sbe.description: The hardware vendor's Solution Builder Extension (SBE) package, its driver and firmware update, is a REQUIREMENT (schema 5.6.4): the package is downloaded and available on a share the automation can read (source_path), for the build and for the first cluster update, which needs it anyway (a vendor whose SBE has no download connector for your cluster reports AdditionalContentRequired; Dell's download is behind a support login). Whether it is required comes from requirement; when that key is absent the vendor catalog (config/oem/<vendor>.json) decides: required for a vendor whose package is a manual download (Dell, HPE, DataON), not required by default where the cluster downloads it itself. Say not_applicable, with not_applicable_reason, for hardware that has no SBE or a cluster that downloads it with the vendor credential. What stays opt-in is only the build-time side-load: nothing is copied to a node unless you set delivery to winrm_copy or node_pull (default skip), and nothing in the toolkit adds a delivery setting or an SBE value to a file. The pre-cluster verification (SB-001 to SB-006) checks that the package on the share is complete, consistent, for the hardware model of every node and validated for the target solution version. The version is the one validated with provisioning.os_version. ARM sbeVersion, sbeFamily, sbePublisher, sbeManifestSource and sbeManifestCreationDate; without a package the ARM deployment passes none of them (nor partnerProperties and partnerCredentiallist), and the template's own empty defaults apply.

publisher.description: Required when hardware.sbe is present and bundle_path is not (nor source_path or requirement; with a package it is read from it). The SBE's publisher, for example Dell.

family.description: Required when hardware.sbe is present and bundle_path is not (nor source_path or requirement). The SBE family of your hardware, for example 16G-45n0c-Intel. With bundle_path it may be empty: it is then read from the package's manifest.

version.description: Required when hardware.sbe is present and bundle_path is not (nor source_path or requirement). The SBE version, for example 5.0.2609.1611, validated with the solution version you install. With bundle_path it may be empty: it is then read from the package's manifest.

manifest_source.description: Where the SBE manifest comes from (a URL or a file path). Only read when an SBE is asked for; the SBE is opt-in and never delivered by default.

manifest_creation_date.description: Creation date of the SBE manifest, as the manifest states it. Only read when an SBE is asked for.

bundle_path.description: Folder on the management host with the OEM's SBE files as downloaded: one SBE_*.zip, its SBE_*.xml and SBE_Discovery_<oem>.xml. Used to prepare machines before Validate. Required when hardware.sbe is present, unless requirement is not_applicable, source_path is set, or publisher, family and version name an SBE you placed in C:\SBE yourself (and needed for any delivery). Same meaning as source_path; when source_path is set it is the one read.

requirement.description: Whether the OEM SBE package is required for this deployment. required: it must be downloaded and available at source_path (the pre-cluster verification fails without it). not_applicable: this hardware has no SBE, or the cluster downloads it with the vendor credential; needs not_applicable_reason. Absent: the vendor catalog (config/oem/<vendor>.json) decides: required for a vendor whose package is a manual download (Dell, HPE, DataON), a Warning that asks you to state it for a vendor whose cluster downloads the package itself (Lenovo Premier), Skipped for a vendor the catalog does not know. This key is about the package being available; whether the toolkit also copies it to the nodes during the build is delivery, a separate opt-in that stays off.

not_applicable_reason.description: Required when requirement is not_applicable: why no package is needed, in one sentence, for example that no SBE exists for the hardware model or that the cluster downloads it with the vendor credential. The gate shows it in its report; an empty reason fails SB-001.

source_path.description: Where the downloaded SBE package is available to the automation: a UNC share or a folder, for example \\server\share\sbe\dell or D:\sbe\dell, that holds the three files as the vendor delivers them: SBE_Discovery_<Vendor>.xml, SBE_<Vendor>_<Family>_<Version>.xml and SBE_<Vendor>_<Family>_<Version>.zip (Microsoft Learn, Import and rediscover updates). Download them before you start: you need them for the first cluster update anyway, and the build can use them too (delivery). The pre-cluster verification reads this location, read only, from the machine that runs the automation, with source_username and source_password when they are set. When it is empty, bundle_path is used. No credential, token or query string in the path (rule AZL-030).

source_username.description: The account that reads source_path when the account running the automation cannot (for example DOMAIN\svc-sbe-read). Read access only. Needs source_password.

source_password.description: The Key Vault secret that holds the password of source_username, as a keyvault://<vault>/<secret> reference. It is read into memory for the run and never written or shown.

package_sha256.description: Optional. The SHA-256 of the payload zip (64 hexadecimal characters), as the vendor publishes it. The gate compares the zip on the share with it and with the PackageHash of the package's discovery manifest; without it the manifest's hash is used.

package_size_bytes.description: Optional. The size of the payload zip in bytes, as downloaded. The gate compares the file on the share with it.

delivery.description: Opt-in (schema 5.4.2): the toolkit side-loads an SBE only when you set winrm_copy or node_pull here; no value means no delivery, and a hardware.sbe block with no delivery copies nothing and touches no C:\SBE. Nothing in the toolkit sets this key for you. How the SBE package reaches the nodes. It lands in each node's C:\SBE during OS configuration. winrm_copy: the toolkit copies the files over WinRM (a PSSession, TCP 5985) from the host it runs on, so that host must reach the nodes' management subnet (the operator host if it can, or a runner that can); needs the nodes' local administrator as -Credential. node_pull: each node downloads the files itself from node_pull_url, a read-only HTTPS or SMB location that you serve from a host the nodes can reach; the toolkit checks the SHA-256 on the node after the download. skip (default, also when the key is absent): the toolkit does not deliver the package, the Sbe step reports it as not delivered (an SBE you configured and placed yourself), and no other step is affected. There is no Azure storage account route: Azure Arc Run Command cannot carry a file.

node_pull_url.description: The folder the nodes pull the SBE files from (delivery node_pull). It is an address the NODES can reach, not necessarily the operator host: https://host/sbe/dell (the three files are fetched by name from it) or a UNC folder \\server\share\sbe (the node reads it as itself, so the share must allow it). Read-only, and it carries no credential: no user name, password, token or query string in the address (rule AZL-030).

allow_unvalidated.description: Test only. Use the SBE in bundle_path even though the OEM's manifest doesn't list it as validated with provisioning.os_version. The hash is still checked. Default false. Documentation only; not read by the tools. The deployment gate fails an SBE the OEM has not validated, whatever this key says.

network_cards.description: The physical network cards in every machine, and what each port is for. A summary of the hardware; from 5.2 each node's ports, with MACs and addresses, are nodes[].network_adapters.

label.description: Where the card sits, as the chassis labels it, for example Slot 6 or Embedded. Documentation only; not read by the tools. A planning input that Trailwright expands into nodes[].network_adapters[], which the tools read.

make.description: Manufacturer of the card. Documentation only; not read by the tools. A planning input that Trailwright expands into nodes[].network_adapters[], which the tools read.

model.description: Model of the card, as the machine reports it. Documentation only; not read by the tools. A planning input that Trailwright expands into nodes[].network_adapters[], which the tools read.

ports.description: The ports of this network card, in the order the vendor numbers them.

name.description: Adapter name in the OS, as the intents use it. Documentation only; not read by the tools. A planning input that Trailwright expands into nodes[].network_adapters[], which the tools read.

speed_gbps.description: Port speed in Gbit/s. Documentation only; not read by the tools. A planning input that Trailwright expands into nodes[].network_adapters[], which the tools read.

rdma.description: RDMA technology the port supports: none, iwarp, roce (RoCE) or roce_v2 (RoCEv2). Documentation only; not read by the tools. A planning input that Trailwright expands into nodes[].network_adapters[], which the tools read.

role.description: unused, intent:<intent name>, cluster:a, cluster:b, iscsi:a or iscsi:b. Documentation only; not read by the tools. A planning input that Trailwright expands into nodes[].network_adapters[], which the tools read.

drives.description: Drives per machine. Get-HardwareInventory.ps1 compares them with the drives the BMC reports and the role (cache or capacity) it works out from the media types.

capacity.description: The capacity drives in each machine (Storage Spaces Direct).

media.description: Media type of the capacity drives: nvme, ssd or hdd.

count.description: Number of capacity drives in each machine.

size_tb.description: Size of one capacity drive in TB (decimal terabytes). Get-HardwareInventory.ps1 compares it with the size the BMC reports (within 5 percent).

cache.description: The cache drives in each machine (Storage Spaces Direct). Leave out when there is no cache tier.

media.description: Media type of the cache drives: nvme, ssd or hdd.

count.description: Number of cache drives in each machine.

size_tb.description: Size of one cache drive in TB (decimal terabytes). Get-HardwareInventory.ps1 compares it with the size the BMC reports (within 5 percent).

management.description: The management network and the infrastructure IP pool. DNS servers can't be changed after deployment.

subnet.description: CIDR. ARM subnetMask is derived from it.

gateway.description: The one default gateway. ARM defaultGateway.

vlan_id.description: 0 means untagged. Can't be changed after deployment. The VLAN the host tags on the management port: simplified provisioning sets it on that port (edge machine networkAdapters[].vlanId). With nodes[].network_adapters the management port's host VLAN (0 when its vlan_mode is access) must match it.

ip_assignment.description: Deprecated in 5.2: set each port's ip_assignment in nodes[].network_adapters. Read when a node has no network_adapters, and must agree with them when both are given (static = static, dhcp = dhcp_reservation or dhcp, preconfigured = preconfigured). How each machine's management address (nodes[].management.ip_address) is set before deployment, on the management port (nodes[].management.mac_address). static (default): the address, the subnet mask, the gateway, the DNS servers and vlan_id are set on that port. Simplified provisioning sets them at the OS install (edge machine siteDetails.deviceConfiguration.network.networkAdapters[], ipAssignmentType Manual, keyed by the MAC); for an ISO install the operator or the toolkit sets them. dhcp: the port stays on DHCP, so reserve each ip_address in DHCP for its MAC. preconfigured: the port is already configured, and the tools don't change it. Not the same as use_dhcp, which is the deployment's ARM useDhcp.

use_dhcp.description: ARM useDhcp: the deployment takes the host and cluster addresses from DHCP instead of static addresses and the infrastructure_pool. Default false. A deployment setting, not how each machine's management port gets its address before deployment: that is ip_assignment.

site_ip_range.description: Simplified provisioning: the address range of the site's network setting (Microsoft.Edge/configurations/networkConfigurations ipv4.addressRange) when the management addresses are static. Default: the lowest to the highest static management address. Inside the management subnet, and holding every static management address.

start.description: First address of the range the site hands out when networking.management.static_method is site (the site network setting Manual). Default: the lowest machine address.

end.description: Last address of the range the site hands out when networking.management.static_method is site. Default: the highest machine address.

provisioning_network.description: Simplified provisioning: how the maintenance environment gets the address it reaches Azure with, on the ports with role provisioning, before the machine is claimed. dhcp (default): a DHCP server answers on that port's network. When the management port is one of those ports, the management network has DHCP (Mode B for a static management port); when it isn't, it is Mode C (Static without management DHCP). static: no DHCP there. A static management port then needs another port with role provisioning and ip_assignment dhcp or dhcp_reservation, or validation stops (AZL-024): Learn documents only the Configurator app for a static maintenance address, and whether the bootable image can carry a preset address is an open research item, so tools don't set it.

static_method.description: Schema 5.3. Simplified provisioning, and only when the management ip_assignment is static: who sets each machine's static management address. device (default): azurelocal-ztp's Device stage sets it on the management port, found by its MAC, through the maintenance environment's Configurator service before the machine is claimed. The Arc site's network setting is then Automatic and the claim carries no Manual adapter. site: the older path. The site's network setting is Manual with an address range (site_ip_range) and Microsoft's OS install assigns the address. Microsoft ignores the MAC there and uses the first ready port, which was observed live on Dell AX-760, so use it only when the first ready port is the management port.

provisioning_dhcp_range.description: Schema 5.3. Simplified provisioning: the DHCP range on the provisioning network (the one the maintenance environment gets its address on). The Device stage scans it (TCP 20001) to find each machine's maintenance environment by MAC when nodes[].maintenance_address isn't set. Inside the management subnet, start at or below end.

start.description: First address of the DHCP pool of the provisioning network. The ZTP Device stage scans the range on TCP 20001 for machines that have no maintenance_address. Default: the start of the management subnet.

end.description: Last address of the DHCP pool of the provisioning network (at most 4096 addresses from the start).

infrastructure_pool.description: At least six contiguous addresses in the management subnet, outside the machines' addresses. ARM startingIPAddress and endingIPAddress.

start.description: First address of the pool the Azure Local infrastructure services use (ARM startingIPAddress): inside the management subnet, outside every machine address and the gateway.

end.description: Last address of the infrastructure pool (ARM endingIPAddress). The pool holds at least 6 contiguous addresses.

oob.description: The out-of-band network of the BMCs. Only subnet is read (by the remote management security profile); gateway and vlan_id are documentation.

subnet.description: Subnet of the out-of-band (BMC) network in CIDR form.

gateway.description: Default gateway of the out-of-band network. Documentation only; not read by the tools. No tool sets the BMC network; only networking.oob.subnet is read.

vlan_id.description: VLAN ID of the out-of-band network; 0 for an untagged port. Documentation only; not read by the tools. No tool sets the BMC network; only networking.oob.subnet is read.

ntp_servers.description: Time sources, as host names or addresses.

name.description: Name of the Network ATC intent, for example management_compute or storage. The same on every machine.

traffic.description: Traffic types the intent carries: management, compute and storage (ARM trafficType). Management and storage can each be in one intent only; compute can be in any number.

adapters.description: Adapters of the intent, by the key nodes[].network_adapters[].name (the port's name in this file, the same on every machine; the file finds the physical adapter by its MAC, so the OS may call it anything). With nodes[].network_adapters (5.2) each name must be a port in every node's list. The name the deployment sends to Azure (ARM intentList adapter) is what the OS calls that adapter on the nodes, found by MAC, or nodes[].network_adapters[].os_name_override when the file sets one. The first adapter matters: the management virtual adapter takes the MAC of the first adapter of the management intent, so that adapter owns the management address.

overrides.description: Network ATC overrides. Leave out to keep Network ATC's defaults, which Microsoft recommends (Learn: 'We recommend that you use the default values'). The deployment sends the adapter overrides on every intent (ARM overrideAdapterProperty true) so Azure's network validation sees the value that is meant: storage intents get RDMA on and a 9014 packet, an intent without storage traffic gets RDMA off and the default 1514 packet. A value given here wins over that default.

qos.description: Data Center Bridging (DCB) quality of service overrides for the storage traffic (ARM qosPolicyOverrides). Leave out to keep Network ATC's validated defaults: cluster priority 7, SMB priority 3, SMB bandwidth 50 percent.

cluster_priority.description: 802.1p priority value of the cluster heartbeat traffic, 0 to 7 (ARM priorityValue8021Action_Cluster). Network ATC default 7. The physical switches must carry the same value.

smb_priority.description: 802.1p priority value of the SMB Direct (RDMA storage) traffic, 0 to 7 (ARM priorityValue8021Action_SMB). Network ATC default 3. The physical switches must carry the same value.

smb_bandwidth_percent.description: Share of the link reserved for SMB Direct storage traffic, 1 to 100 percent (ARM bandwidthPercentage_SMB). Network ATC default 50.

adapter.description: Physical adapter property overrides (ARM adapterPropertyOverrides: jumboPacket, networkDirect, networkDirectTechnology). Microsoft: change these only on OEM guidance and validate them with the OEM.

jumbo_packet.description: Value of the adapter's JumboPacket property in bytes: 1514 (standard frame), 4088 or 9014 (jumbo). The ARM parameter takes it as a string. Leave out for the default this tool sets: 9014 on an intent that carries storage traffic, 1514 on any other. Learn recommends a maximum transmission unit of 9216 bytes on the physical switches for RDMA storage traffic and the same MTU end to end on hosts and switches; for an external SAN storage fabric use the MTU your storage vendor specifies.

network_direct.description: RDMA (Network Direct) on the adapters of this intent. true is sent to ARM as networkDirect 'Enabled', false as 'Disabled'. Leave out for the default this tool sets: on for an intent that carries storage traffic, off for any other. Set false to disable RDMA, for example when you test in virtual machines.

network_direct_technology.description: RDMA technology of the adapters: iwarp, roce_v2 (RoCEv2) or roce (RoCE, version 1). Sent to ARM as networkDirectTechnology 'iWARP', 'RoCEv2' or 'RoCE'; Learn's network considerations name RoCEv2 and iWARP, the ARM model also accepts RoCE. Used only when network_direct is on; leave out for RoCEv2. Set the technology your adapter vendor and switches are configured for.

virtual_switch.description: Virtual switch overrides of the intent's switch-embedded team (ARM virtualSwitchConfigurationOverrides). Leave out for Network ATC's defaults.

enable_iov.description: SR-IOV on the intent's virtual switch (ARM enableIov). Cannot be changed after the switch exists.

load_balancing_algorithm.description: Load balancing of the switch-embedded team: dynamic or hyper_v_port (ARM loadBalancingAlgorithm 'Dynamic' or 'HyperVPort').

storage.description: Storage networks (Storage Spaces Direct). ARM storageNetworkList, enableStorageAutoIp and storageConnectivitySwitchless.

auto_ip.description: Network ATC assigns the storage addresses. When false, each node lists its storage_ips. Default true.

switchless_links.description: Switchless only: one or two links between each pair of machines. Documentation only; not read by the tools. Derived from networking.storage.networks[] and nodes[].storage_ips (one subnet per link).

tor_switches.description: Top-of-rack switches. Documentation only; not read by the tools. Derived from the entries of network_devices[] with type switch.

layout.description: dedicated: storage on its own ports. converged: storage shares ports with other traffic. Documentation only; not read by the tools. Derived from networking.intents[].traffic: a storage-only intent is dedicated, storage with other traffic is converged.

networks.description: The storage networks (SMB), one per storage adapter. The adapter is named by the key nodes[].network_adapters[].name, the same on every machine.

name.description: For example StorageNetwork1.

adapter.description: The adapter of this storage network, by the key nodes[].network_adapters[].name (the same on every machine). The name the deployment sends to Azure (storageNetworkList networkAdapterName) is what the OS calls that adapter, found by MAC, or its os_name_override.

cluster_network_properties.description: Schema 5.6.10. Disaggregated (SAN) only: the adapter properties of the cluster networks (ARM sanNetworkList.clusterNetworkConfig.adapterProperties). The defaults are the values of Microsoft's quickstart template.

bandwidth_percentage_smb.description: Share of the bandwidth reserved for SMB traffic (CSV and live migration), 1 to 97 percent. ARM bandwidthPercentageSmb.

jumbo_packet.description: Value of the JumboPacket property of the cluster network adapters, in bytes: 1514 (standard frame), 4088 or 9014 (jumbo). ARM jumboPacket.

priority_cluster.description: 802.1p priority of the cluster heartbeat traffic, 0 to 7. ARM priorityValue8021ActionCluster.

priority_smb.description: 802.1p priority of the SMB traffic, 0 to 7. ARM priorityValue8021ActionSmb.

cluster_networks.description: Disaggregated (SAN) only: the cluster networks on standalone ports, fabric A and B. ARM sanNetworkList.

name.description: Name of the cluster network on a standalone port (fabric A or B of a SAN design), for example clusterNetwork-A. ARM sanNetworkList name.

adapter.description: The port of this cluster network, by the key nodes[].network_adapters[].name (the same on every machine).

vlan_id.description: VLAN of this cluster network, 0 to 4094. 0 means untagged.

subnet.description: Subnet of this cluster network in CIDR form.

purpose.description: What the network is for (since 5.6). management and oob mark a network the machines' remote management may be reached from: the remote management security profile adds its subnet to the allowed sources of dev and production (a candidate, not a trust: prefer listing the controller addresses in os_configuration.remoting.allowed_source_cidrs). automation, compute, storage and other have no effect on remote management.

vlans.description: Every VLAN in the design, by name.

name.description: Name of the VLAN, for example storage-1. The intents and the storage networks refer to the number, not to the name.

id.description: The VLAN number, 1 to 4094. The pre-cluster verification compares it with the VLANs the switch ports are meant to allow.

subnet.description: Subnet that runs in this VLAN, in CIDR form. When the purpose is management or oob, the remote management security profile treats the subnet as a source the machines may be reached from.

purpose.description: Free text. The values management, oob, automation, compute, storage and other (any case) are the purpose marker: management and oob make the subnet a candidate source for the remote management security profile of dev and production. Any other text has no effect.

logical_networks.description: Arc VM logical networks created after deployment (task phase-06 task-08, New-LogicalNetwork.ps1: az stack-hci-vm network lnet create). Also read by the remote management security profile (purpose, address_prefix) and by the pre-cluster verification (name, vlan_id, address_prefix, purpose). The older form networking.onprem.logical_networks[] (default_gateway, ip_pools) is deprecated. A Static network needs address_prefix, gateway, dns_servers, vlan_id and ip_pool (Learn: DNS server, gateway and VLAN ID must be specified for a static logical network). Microsoft Learn: once a logical network exists you cannot change its gateway, IP pool, address space, VLAN ID or virtual switch name, so the script never changes an existing one.

name.description: Name of the Azure Local logical network resource.

enabled.description: false skips this logical network when the logical networks are created, without removing it from the file. Default true. (Since 5.6.3.)

ip_allocation_method.description: How machines on this logical network get addresses: Static (the ip_pool is used; address_prefix is needed) or Dynamic (DHCP). Default Static. ARM and az stack-hci-vm: ipAllocationMethod. (Since 5.6.3.)

nsg_name.description: Name of the network security group to associate with the logical network. The association is made when the logical network is created, so create the group first (networking.network_security_groups[], New-NetworkSecurityGroup.ps1): the name must be one of that list, and sdn.enabled must be true. Leave it out for a logical network without a group. The script does not associate a group with a logical network that exists. (Since 5.6.3.)

vm_switch_name.description: Name of the external virtual switch on the cluster that this logical network is created on (az stack-hci-vm: --vm-switch-name; it cannot be changed afterwards). Leave it out: the script reads the external virtual switches of the cluster with Get-VMSwitch -SwitchType External, the command Microsoft Learn gives, and uses the one it finds. Name it only when the cluster has more than one external switch (for example one for each compute intent); the name must be one the cluster reports. Network ATC names the switch after the intent, but the script does not build a name from the intent.

purpose.description: What the network is for (since 5.6). management and oob mark a network the machines' remote management may be reached from: the remote management security profile adds its subnet to the allowed sources of dev and production (a candidate, not a trust: prefer listing the controller addresses in os_configuration.remoting.allowed_source_cidrs). automation, compute, storage and other have no effect on remote management.

vlan_id.description: VLAN ID of the logical network; 0 for untagged. Needed when ip_allocation_method is Static (Learn: DNS server, gateway and VLAN ID must be specified for a static logical network). For a Dynamic network, leave it out for 0.

address_prefix.description: Address prefix of the logical network in CIDR form. Needed when ip_allocation_method is Static (az stack-hci-vm takes one prefix). Not used for a Dynamic network; it is still read by the remote management security profile and the pre-cluster verification.

gateway.description: Default gateway of the logical network, inside address_prefix. Needed when ip_allocation_method is Static (Learn: gateway, DNS server and VLAN ID must be specified for a static logical network). Not used for a Dynamic network.

dns_servers.description: DNS servers handed to machines on this logical network (az stack-hci-vm: --dns-servers). Needed when ip_allocation_method is Static; not used for a Dynamic network.

ip_pool.description: The one address range Azure Local hands to virtual machines on this logical network (first and last address, both inside address_prefix), sent as --ip-pool-start and --ip-pool-end. Needed when ip_allocation_method is Static. The pool type is not a key: Learn's static examples give none. Not used for a Dynamic network.

start.description: First address of the pool that virtual machines on this logical network draw from.

network_security_groups.description: Schema 5.6.11. Network security groups (NSG) for Azure Local virtual machines and logical networks, with their rules. New-NetworkSecurityGroup.ps1 (phase 06, task 07: az stack-hci-vm network nsg create and nsg rule create) creates each group and the rules it does not have yet. NSGs on Azure Local need SDN enabled by Azure Arc (sdn.enabled true); the script does not turn SDN on and refuses a file that lists a group while SDN is off. Run it before New-LogicalNetwork.ps1: a logical network is tied to its group when the logical network is created (networking.logical_networks[].nsg_name). Microsoft Learn: a group must have at least one rule, because an empty group denies all inbound traffic and a machine or logical network that uses it cannot be reached; the script refuses a group without rules. No Az PowerShell cmdlet creates these groups, so the script uses the Azure CLI with the stack-hci-vm extension.

name.description: Name of the network security group, 1 to 80 characters: letters, digits, underscore, period and hyphen; it starts with a letter or digit and ends with a letter, digit or underscore (Learn: naming rules for Microsoft.Network). It cannot be changed afterwards.

rules.description: The security rules of the group. At least one is needed. The script creates the rules that are missing; a rule that exists (same name) is left alone and, when it differs from the file, reported.

name.description: Name of the rule, 1 to 80 characters, with the same characters as the group name. Unique inside the group.

priority.description: Priority of the rule, 100 to 4096. Unique inside the group. A lower number is evaluated first. Leave gaps between the numbers for rules you add later.

direction.description: Whether the rule applies to incoming (Inbound) or outgoing (Outbound) traffic. To control both directions, write two rules.

access.description: Allow or Deny the traffic the rule matches.

protocol.description: Protocol the rule matches: * (any, the default), Tcp, Udp or Icmp (az stack-hci-vm network nsg rule create --protocol). The script accepts any letter case.

source_address_prefixes.description: Source addresses the rule matches: * (any, the default), an IPv4 address or an IPv4 range in CIDR form. A list. Service tags are not used on Azure Local.

destination_address_prefixes.description: Destination addresses the rule matches: * (any, the default), an IPv4 address or an IPv4 range in CIDR form. A list.

source_port_ranges.description: Source ports the rule matches: * (any, the default), a port or a range such as 1024-2048, each from 0 to 65535. A list.

destination_port_ranges.description: Destination ports the rule matches: * (any), a port or a range such as 8000-8100, each from 0 to 65535. A list. Required: the Azure CLI default is port 80, which is not a default to rely on.

description.description: Optional text for the rule, at most 140 characters. The characters & | < > ^ % and the double quote are not allowed: the Azure CLI is started through a command file on Windows, which treats them as commands.

proxy.description: Proxy server for the machines' outbound traffic, for scenario.outbound_path proxy or proxy_arc_gateway. The OS configuration passes url and bypass to the Arc registration of a machine installed from an ISO (Invoke-AzStackHciArcInitialization -Proxy and -ProxyBypass).

url.description: URL of the proxy server, for example http://proxy.example.test:3128. A plain proxy: no PAC file and no credentials. Passed to the Arc registration as -Proxy.

bypass.description: Addresses and names that go direct, not through the proxy. Learn (Register Azure Local with Azure Arc): include the address and the NetBIOS name of each machine and of the cluster, and the infrastructure addresses; use localhost, not <local>; use a wildcard such as 192.168.1.* for a subnet (no CIDR) and *.example.test for a domain. Passed to the Arc registration as -ProxyBypass, joined with commas.

arc_gateway.description: The Arc gateway resource, in the same subscription as the machines.

name.description: Name of the Azure Arc gateway resource (Azure public cloud only; not supported with simplified machine provisioning in the preview).

resource_group.description: Resource group of the Azure Arc gateway resource.

private_path.description: Outbound path over a private connection (ExpressRoute or site-to-site VPN) when scenario.outbound_path is private_path. The Azure Firewall explicit proxy is the machines' proxy server: the OS configuration passes firewall_private_ip and firewall_port, and proxy_bypass, to the Arc registration of a machine installed from an ISO. The Arc gateway of networking.outbound.arc_gateway is passed too. The network side (virtual network, subnets, Private Link Scope, transport) is a record of the design that Trailwright writes.

transport.description: The private connection: expressroute or site_to_site_vpn. Documentation only; not read by the tools: the connection is built outside the toolkit.

virtual_network.description: Name of the Azure virtual network of the private path. Documentation only; not read by the tools: the network is built outside the toolkit.
