workload_subnet.description: Name of the workload subnet of that virtual network. Documentation only; not read by the tools.

firewall_subnet.description: Name of the firewall subnet of that virtual network. Documentation only; not read by the tools.

firewall_private_ip.description: Private address of the Azure Firewall on that path. The OS configuration passes it, with firewall_port, as the proxy server of the Arc registration: http://<address>:<port> (Invoke-AzStackHciArcInitialization -Proxy). Learn: the Azure Firewall internal IP and port as the proxy server.

firewall_port.description: TCP port of the Azure Firewall explicit proxy on that path (it proxies HTTP and HTTPS). Passed with firewall_private_ip as the proxy server of the Arc registration.

arc_private_link_scope.description: true when the machines reach Azure Arc through an Azure Arc Private Link Scope on that path. Documentation only; not read by the tools. Learn: Azure Local does not support an Arc Private Link Scope on the virtual network where Azure Firewall runs as explicit proxy.

proxy_bypass.description: Host names and address ranges that bypass the proxy on this path. Passed to the Arc registration as -ProxyBypass, joined with commas. Same rules as networking.outbound.proxy.bypass: localhost, not <local>; a wildcard for a subnet or a domain, no CIDR; no .svc (the registration script handles it).

local_admin.description: The deployment's local administrator on every machine. Not the built-in Administrator: the deployment renames it. ARM localAdminUserName and localAdminPassword.

username.description: User name of the deployment local administrator on every machine (ARM localAdminUserName). Not Administrator or Guest: the deployment renames the built-in account.

username_secret.description: Optional. The Key Vault secret that holds this user name, as a keyvault://<vault>/<secret> reference, for the tools that read the user name from the vault (azurelocal-ztp's Add-KeyVaultCredentials.ps1 stores it as local-admin-username next to the password). The pre-cluster verification (IDN-016) reads it and fails when it differs from username. Default: the secret local-admin-username in the vault of the password reference; a default secret that does not exist is a warning, a secret named here that does not exist is a failure. (since 5.6)

password.description: At least 14 characters with lowercase, uppercase, a digit and a special character.

local_identity.description: Local identity with Key Vault. The instance's secrets go to cluster.key_vault.

dns_zone.description: DNS zone of the local identity instance, for example the zone the identity endpoints are published in. Used when dns_server_config is use_dns_server.

dns_forwarders.description: DNS servers the identity instance forwards to. Used when dns_server_config is use_forwarder (ARM UseForwarder).

entra.description: Entra ID groups, role assignments and PIM.

groups.description: Entra ID groups the instance expects. New-EntraSecurityGroups.ps1 creates them and Set-EntraGroupRoleAssignments.ps1 assigns their roles.

name.description: Display name of the Entra ID group.

purpose.description: What the group is for, in words.

roles.description: Azure role names assigned to the group.

active_directory.description: The Active Directory the instance joins and its accounts. Applies when scenario.identity is active_directory.

ou_path.description: Distinguished name of the dedicated OU. ARM adouPath. https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/deploy/deployment-prep-active-directory

lcm_user.description: The LCM deployment user, created in the OU by the AD preparation module. ARM AzureStackLCMAdminUsername and AzureStackLCMAdminPassword.

username.description: Name only, no domain. Up to 20 characters.

password.description: At least 14 characters with lowercase, uppercase, a digit and a special character.

domain_join_account.description: Optional override. The OS configuration run joins each machine to the domain (Add-Computer) before the cluster validation and deployment with the LCM user (lcm_user), which Microsoft's Active Directory preparation gives the right to create and delete computer objects in the dedicated OU and which is the account used for domain-join actions. Set this only when your site joins machines with another account; it needs the same rights on ou_path. (since 5.5)

username.description: The join account: a name (svc-azl-join, qualified with netbios_name), NETBIOS\name or name@domain. (since 5.5)

password.description: A Key Vault secret reference. The toolkit reads it on the machine that runs the OS configuration, passes it to the node as a secret and never writes it to disk, a log, the event feed or the report. (since 5.5)

local_admin_members.description: Domain principals the OS configuration adds to the local Administrators group of every machine after the join and the restart, so a domain account can be used for remoting and log access (a domain account is not a local administrator by default; the deployment adds the LCM user itself later). Names without the domain; users and groups. Default: the security_groups entries whose purpose says they administer the instance, and the LCM user. (since 5.5)

join_options.description: How the OS configuration run joins the machines to the domain. Optional. (since 5.5)

allow_ou_move.description: true: before the deployment, a machine already joined to this domain but sitting in another OU is moved into ou_path. false (default): it is reported as blocked and left where it is. Microsoft does not support moving the computer objects to another OU after the deployment, so a machine that is already part of a cluster is never moved, whatever this says. (since 5.5)

domain_controllers.description: Addresses of domain controllers, for pre-checks and for the domain join. They must be the DNS servers of the management port (rule AZL-052): the machines find the domain through them.

use_gmsa.description: Whether the instance uses group managed service accounts. Default false. Learn 2610 does not require a KDS root key for Azure Local (the Active Directory preparation never mentions one); a KDS root key matters only for gMSA, so the pre-cluster verification (ID-AD-012) checks it only when this is true. (since 5.6)

dns_secure_dynamic_updates.description: Whether the DNS servers of the management network support secure dynamic updates (Microsoft DNS integrated with Active Directory). true: the node, cluster (CNO) and client access point (VCO) host records are created when the machines join, so a missing record is only a warning in the pre-cluster verification. false: Learn requires the Host (A) records before the deployment, so a missing record fails it. Default when not set: true when every DNS server is one of domain_controllers, else false. (since 5.6)

security_groups.description: Groups created in the OU for administration of the instance.

name.description: Name of the security group in Active Directory.

purpose.description: What the group is for, in words. The OS configuration reads local_groups, not this text.

members.description: Members of the group, as account names (sAMAccountName or user principal name).

local_groups.description: The local groups of every machine this AD group is added to after the deployment (for example Administrators, Remote Management Users). Empty or missing: the group is not added to any local group (WAC groups are applied on the WAC server only). Read by the post-deployment task that applies the security groups and by the Ansible AD preparation role.

storage.description: Storage of the instance: the deployment's storage mode, the volumes, and the SAN of a disaggregated or hybrid deployment (the san block applies only when scenario.storage_architecture is san or hybrid).

configuration_mode.description: ARM configurationMode: express (Express), infra_only (InfraOnly) or keep_storage (KeepStorage).

pool.description: Schema 5.6.9. The Storage Spaces Direct pool of the instance. Read by New-StorageVolume.ps1 (phase 06, task 05).

name.description: Name of the storage pool the volumes are created in. Leave it out: the script then uses the one Storage Spaces Direct pool the cluster has (an Azure Local deployment names it SU1_Pool). Needed only when the cluster has more than one pool.

thin_provisioning_alert_threshold_percen.description: Share of the pool, in percent, at which Azure Local raises the thin provisioning alert (Set-StoragePool -ThinProvisioningAlertThresholds). Microsoft's default is 70 and Microsoft recommends keeping it. Leave it out and the script does not touch the setting.

csv.description: Schema 5.6.9. Cluster shared volume settings of the instance. Read by New-StorageVolume.ps1 (phase 06, task 05).

read_cache_size_mib.description: Memory per machine, in MiB, for the CSV in-memory read cache (the cluster property BlockCacheSize). Azure Local has it on with 1024 by default; 0 switches it off; up to 80 percent of the memory of a machine can be used. Leave it out and the script does not touch the setting. A change takes effect when the volumes next move or come online.

volumes.description: The Storage Spaces Direct volumes to create after deployment, in addition to what the deployment itself creates (storage.configuration_mode). New-StorageVolume.ps1 (phase 06, task 05) creates each one that does not exist yet with New-Volume and never changes or removes one that exists. Not used with scenario.storage_architecture san.

name.description: Name of the volume, for example vol-workloads-01. It becomes the folder C:\ClusterStorage\<name>. Not a name the deployment manages (UserStorage_<n>, Infrastructure_<n>).

size_gib.description: Size of the volume in GiB (binary units, as Windows counts).

resiliency.description: Resiliency of the volume. two_way, three_way and parity (dual parity, 4 or more machines) are the usual ones; four_way is for a rack aware cluster; nested_two_way and nested_mirror_accelerated_parity are for a cluster of two machines; mirror_accelerated_parity needs 4 or more machines and ReFS (the two accelerated-parity values are new in 5.6.9). Leave it out and Storage Spaces Direct chooses: two-way mirror with one or two machines, three-way mirror with three or more.

provisioning_type.description: Schema 5.6.9. thin (space is taken from the pool as data is written) or fixed (all space is taken when the volume is created). Leave it out and the default of the pool applies. For a volume made of storage tiers (nested or accelerated parity) the script sets this on the tier templates of the pool for the creation, as Microsoft Learn describes, and puts the templates back afterwards.

file_system.description: Schema 5.6.9. refs (the default; Microsoft recommends it for all volumes, and mirror-accelerated parity and ReFS deduplication need it) or ntfs.

parity_percent.description: Schema 5.6.9. Only for mirror_accelerated_parity and nested_mirror_accelerated_parity: the share of the volume, in percent, that is parity; the rest is mirror. The default is 80, the ratio Microsoft recommends for most workloads.

media_type.description: Schema 5.6.9. ssd or hdd: the capacity drives the volume goes on, when the machines have both kinds. NVMe counts as ssd. Leave it out on machines with one kind of capacity drive; for a volume made of storage tiers the script then takes it from hardware.drives.capacity.media.

deduplication.description: Schema 5.6.9. ReFS deduplication and compression of the volume. Off unless type says otherwise.

type.description: none (the default: the script does not touch deduplication), dedup, compress or dedup_and_compress (Enable-ReFSDedup -Type). Needs file_system refs. The script turns it on for a volume that has it off and never changes or turns off what is already set.

schedule.description: When the deduplication job runs (Set-ReFSDedupSchedule). Give all three keys or leave the block out; without a schedule a job runs only when someone starts one.

start_time.description: Time of day the job starts, as HH:mm in the time of the machines, for example 22:00.

days.description: The days the job runs: Sunday to Saturday, or EveryDay.

duration_hours.description: The longest one run may take, in hours.

paths.description: Schema 5.6.9. The Azure Local storage paths to create after deployment: the Azure resources that say where on a cluster shared volume the virtual machine files, images and disks go. New-StoragePath.ps1 (phase 06, task 05) creates each one that does not exist yet in azure.resource_group, on azure.custom_location, with the file-level tags. The storage paths the deployment makes in Express mode are not listed here.

name.description: Name of the storage path resource: 3 to 64 letters, digits or hyphens. It cannot be renamed later.

path.description: The folder on a cluster shared volume, for example C:\ClusterStorage\vol-workloads-01\vms for a volume of storage.volumes, or the folder of the cluster shared volume of a SAN LUN. Never on the infrastructure volume. It cannot be changed later.

vm_images.description: Schema 5.6.11. The Azure Marketplace images to download to the instance as Azure Local VM images (Learn: Create Azure Local VM image using Azure Marketplace images). New-VmImage.ps1 (phase 06, task 06) creates each image that does not exist yet in azure.resource_group, on azure.custom_location, in azure.location, with the file-level tags. An image that exists is left alone; a failed one is reported, never deleted. Needs the Microsoft.EdgeMarketplace resource provider registered in the subscription and the Azure Connected Machine Resource Manager role for the Microsoft.AzureStackHCI resource provider app on the resource group. Only Azure Marketplace images are supported: images from a local path, a storage account, an existing virtual machine or an Azure compute gallery are not (they need image preparation that this file does not describe). The list lives in storage because an image is kept on a storage path of the instance.

name.description: Name of the VM image resource, 1 to 80 characters: letters, digits, hyphen, period and underscore; it starts and ends with a letter or digit. It cannot be renamed. Learn: a newer Marketplace image is a new image with a new name (the portal increments the number), so pin the version in the name if you keep several.

os_type.description: Operating system of the image, Windows or Linux (az stack-hci-vm image create --os-type). The images in Learn's Marketplace table are Windows images; for a Linux image Learn describes other procedures (Red Hat Enterprise Linux and Ubuntu: prepare the image, export the disk).

publisher.description: Publisher of the Marketplace image, as Learn's table gives it (lowercase).

version.description: Version of the Marketplace image, for example 26100.4652.250808, or latest (the default: Azure picks the newest version when the image is created, and the script reports which). The script never writes the version it finds back to this file.

storage_path.description: Name of the storage path the image is kept on, one of storage.paths[].name; create it first (New-StoragePath.ps1). Leave it out and Azure Local chooses a storage path itself (Learn: Choose automatically).

san.description: The external SAN of a disaggregated (san) or hybrid deployment. Its presence, and scenario.storage_architecture san or hybrid, tell the solution there is a SAN; type says fibre_channel or iscsi, and the OS configuration does the host-side MPIO and MSDSM work from that (type, array.vendor and array.model are all it needs). From 5.3 it also records the array, the Fibre Channel fabrics and target WWPNs or the iSCSI targets, which the SAN deployment and zoning work read; each machine's own HBAs or initiator are nodes[].san.

type.description: Whether the SAN is fibre_channel or iscsi. This selects the OS configuration's host-side steps: fibre_channel registers the array's MSDSM hardware ID (config/san/msdsm-vendors.json), CLAIMS it for MPIO (mpclaim -n -i -d with the vendor padded to 8 and the product padded to 16 characters, which puts it in MPIOSupportedDeviceList; the MSDSM registration alone is not enough, Azure Local already ships PURE FlashArray registered and the paths stayed separate), sets the load balance policy and the vendor MPIO settings, collects the WWPNs (Get-InitiatorPort) and restarts so MPIO claims the paths, then checks each LUN is seen once and listed by mpclaim -s -d; iscsi does the same and also starts the MSiSCSI service, enables MSDSM auto-claim for iSCSI and makes the target portals and sessions from storage.san.iscsi (not for scenario.storage_architecture san on Azure Local 2610 or later: the deployment configures iSCSI there and Microsoft Learn says not to enable it by hand before it; the release is deployment.solution_version, else the ZTP handoff). Only type, and the array vendor and model (storage.san.array), are needed for the host-side work; the target WWPNs and the nodes' HBA WWPNs are needed later, for zoning and LUN masking (with fibre_channel, do not zone the HBA WWNs until after the Azure Local deployment).

array.description: Schema 5.3. The storage array that presents the LUNs.

name.description: The array's name, for example its hostname in the array manager. Documentation only; not read by the tools.

vendor.description: Vendor of the storage array, for example Dell or Pure Storage. The OS configuration matches it with the array's MPIO vendor and product id when it claims the array.

model.description: Model of the storage array, for example PowerStore 1200T.

management_address.description: The array's management address. Documentation only; not read by the tools: no tool signs in to the array.

fibre_channel.description: Schema 5.3. Used when type is fibre_channel: the fabrics and the array's target ports, for zoning. Optional for the OS configuration's host-side work (MPIO needs only type and the array vendor and model); a hybrid file may leave it out until the zoning is planned. Each machine's HBA ports are nodes[].san.hbas.

fabrics.description: The Fibre Channel fabrics, for example A and B. Every WWPN names one by fabric.

name.description: For example A or B. Unique. Documentation only; not read by the tools. Only the validator reads it, to check the fabric references; zoning is done on the SAN switch, not by the toolkit.

switch.description: The fabric's switch, for example a network_devices[].hostname. Documentation only; not read by the tools: zoning is done on the switch.

zone_set.description: The active zone set on this fabric. Documentation only; not read by the tools: zoning is done on the switch.

target_wwpns.description: The array's target ports (WWPNs) and the fabric each is cabled to. Zoning lets each machine's HBA ports see them.

wwpn.description: A Fibre Channel World Wide Port Name: 16 hexadecimal digits, as 8 colon-separated pairs (50:00:09:72:08:12:34:56) or without colons. Documentation only; not read by the tools. A zoning record of the array side; Azure Local takes no target WWPN (it finds the volumes by storage.san.luns[].unique_id).

fabric.description: A name in fabrics. Documentation only; not read by the tools. A zoning record of the array side; Azure Local takes no target WWPN.

iscsi.description: Schema 5.3. Used when type is iscsi: the array's targets and CHAP. For a hybrid design, or a san design before Azure Local 2610, the OS configuration makes a target portal and a session (persistent, multipath) from every iscsi:a / iscsi:b port of every machine to every portal of every target (a target with a fabric A or B is reached only from the port with the matching role); with CHAP enabled it makes none and says so. Each machine's initiator IQN is nodes[].san.initiator_iqn; the addresses of its iSCSI ports are on nodes[].network_adapters with role iscsi:a and iscsi:b.

portals.description: The target portals: an IPv4 address, optionally with a port (default 3260), for example 198.51.100.10 or 198.51.100.10:3260.

fabric.description: The storage network this target serves, matching the iSCSI port role: A for iscsi:a, B for iscsi:b.

chap.description: CHAP authentication of the sessions. The secret is a Key Vault reference.

enabled.description: true when the iSCSI targets require CHAP. The OS configuration then makes the target portals but not the sessions (CHAP sessions need the secret, which no tool reads yet) and says so in its plan.

username.description: CHAP user name for the iSCSI targets. ARM chapUsername of the iSCSI deployment.

secret.description: A secret reference, for example keyvault://<vault>/<secret> (a keyvault:// vault must be listed in key_vaults). The deployment sends it as the secure parameter chapCredential of the iSCSI template. With chap.mutual true the template uses this one secret for both directions: Microsoft's create-cluster-san-iscsi template has no second (target) secret parameter, so there is no key for one.

mutual.description: Schema 5.6.10. true: the initiators also authenticate the targets (ARM chapType Mutual); false: one-way CHAP (OneWay). With enabled false the deployment gets chapType None. Microsoft's template uses the one CHAP credential for both directions.

jumbo_packet.description: Schema 5.6.10. Value of the JumboPacket property of the iSCSI ports, in bytes: 1514 (standard frame), 4088 or 9014 (jumbo). Use the same frame size on the whole iSCSI path. ARM iScsiNetworkConfig.adapterProperties.jumboPacket.

networks.description: Schema 5.6.10. The iSCSI networks, one per path. The iSCSI ports are dedicated physical ports outside the network intents; a port belongs to a path by its role iscsi:a or iscsi:b (nodes[].network_adapters[].roles). The iSCSI deployment reads this (ARM iScsiNetworkConfig.adapterIPConfig).

fabric.description: The path: A for the ports with the role iscsi:a, B for iscsi:b.

vlan_id.description: VLAN of this iSCSI network, 0 to 4094. 0 means untagged (the switch port is an access port).

subnet.description: Subnet of this iSCSI network in CIDR form.

next_hop.description: Only when the target portals of this path are in another subnet: the router address on this network. The deployment then reaches each portal of the path through it. Leave it out when the portals are in the subnet: each portal is then sent as its own next hop, as in the template of Microsoft. The iSCSI ports never get a default gateway.

infra_volume_lun_id.description: LUN of the infrastructure volume (250 GB minimum). ARM infraVolLunId.

performance_history_lun_id.description: LUN of the performance history volume (20 GB minimum). ARM infraPerfLunId.

luns.description: The LUNs the array presents to the cluster for workload volumes, after the deployment. New-SanVolume.ps1 (phase 06, task 05) prepares each one that is not a Cluster Shared Volume yet: it finds the disk by unique_id, brings it online, initializes it as GPT, creates one NTFS partition with 64 KB allocation units, adds it to the failover cluster as a disk named name and adds it to the CSVs. It never changes a disk that has a partition or data. Not the LUNs of the infrastructure and performance history volumes (infra_volume_lun_id, performance_history_lun_id): the deployment owns those.

name.description: Name of the LUN. It becomes the name of the cluster disk and of the Cluster Shared Volume, so it is the name you see in Failover Cluster Manager and in Get-ClusterSharedVolume. Use the name the array shows, so the two match. 1 to 63 letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen, unique in the list; not UserStorage_<n> or Infrastructure_<n>. New-SanVolume.ps1 reads it.

unique_id.description: Schema 5.6.16. The UniqueId of the disk this LUN shows on the machines, as Get-Disk reports it (Learn: Connect an external storage array to Azure Local, step 7: use UniqueId as the authoritative identifier; it is the same on every machine, disk numbers are not). Find it with Get-Disk | Select-Object Number, SerialNumber, UniqueId, or on the array (the LUN's NAA or WWN). New-SanVolume.ps1 finds the disk only by this value, never by size or disk number, and does nothing to a LUN that has none.

size_gib.description: Size of the LUN in GiB (binary units, as Windows counts). New-SanVolume.ps1 compares it with the size of the disk and refuses a disk that differs by more than 1 percent.

lun_id.description: The logical unit number the array presents the LUN as, for example 2. New-SanVolume.ps1 compares it with the LUN number the disk shows (the Location of Get-Disk, when it shows one) and refuses a disk where they differ. It never picks a disk by it.

security.description: Security settings of the deployment. Omitted settings take Microsoft's recommended defaults.

drift_control.description: true turns drift control on: Azure Local resets the security settings to the baseline after drift. Part of the cluster security settings of the deployment.

credential_guard.description: true turns Credential Guard on in the security settings of the deployment.

smb_signing.description: true turns SMB signing on in the security settings of the deployment.

smb_cluster_encryption.description: true encrypts SMB traffic between the cluster nodes (not the storage traffic).

bitlocker_boot_volume.description: true turns BitLocker on for the boot volume.

bitlocker_data_volumes.description: true turns BitLocker on for the data volumes.

wdac.description: true turns Windows Defender Application Control on.

baseline_settings.description: Schema 5.6.21. Individual security baseline settings to change after the deployment, by Set-AzsSecurity (Azure Local 2610 or later). Drift control stays on and protects the value you set instead of the baseline value. Set-SecurityBaselines.ps1 (stage 05, phase 04, task 03) applies each entry to the whole instance (-Cluster, the way Microsoft Learn recommends: the change is recorded as cluster policy intent and survives solution updates). Only Set-AzsSecurity may change these settings: Group Policy or the registry is not supported and drift control reverts it. Some settings cannot be changed at all (Learn lists them); the script refuses them. The names come from the security baseline CSV of your version (the Name column), which Learn links under View and download security settings. Empty or missing: the script does nothing.

type.description: Schema 5.6.21. The policy type that owns the setting (the -Type parameter of Set-AzsSecurity): SecuritySettings (the OS security baseline: registry, security policy, audit policy and user rights settings; most changes), SecuredCore (virtualization-based security, hypervisor-enforced code integrity, System Guard launch) or DefenderAntivirus (Microsoft Defender Antivirus configuration).

name.description: Schema 5.6.21. The name of the setting exactly as the Name column of the security baseline CSV writes it (-SettingName); the cmdlet does not complete or correct names. For example LanmanWorkstationEnableInsecureGuestLogons.

value.description: Schema 5.6.21. The value to set: a string, an integer (sent as a string) or a list of strings. What a setting accepts is in the baseline CSV; the cmdlet rejects a value it cannot use.

acknowledge_weaker_security.description: Schema 5.6.21. true confirms that you understand a change that weakens the security posture, for the few settings where Set-AzsSecurity shows a warning and asks (the script then passes -Force, together with -Confirm:$false, as Learn describes for unattended use). false or missing: such a setting is not changed and is reported as Failed with the cmdlet's warning. Blocked settings cannot be changed with it.

defender_for_cloud.description: The free level of Microsoft Defender for Cloud that Azure Local needs to show its security settings in the Azure portal. Enable-DefenderForCloud.ps1 reads it. No paid plan is turned on by any key of this file.

enabled.description: true (default) registers the Microsoft.Security resource provider on the subscription of the cluster, which turns on Foundational CSPM, the free plan. false leaves Defender for Cloud alone.

apply_cloud_security_benchmark.description: true (default) assigns the Microsoft cloud security benchmark initiative to the subscription of the cluster when it is not assigned yet. Free. Without it the security settings of Azure Local do not show in the portal.

security_contact_email.description: Address that Microsoft Defender for Cloud sends its security notifications to (a team mailbox; several addresses are separated by semicolons). Free. Empty or absent sets no contact. Enable-DefenderForCloud.ps1 sets it when the subscription has no security contact yet, and never replaces one that exists.

telemetry.description: What the cluster sends to Microsoft as telemetry. Not read by the tools yet.

streaming_data.description: true sends the streaming diagnostic data.

episodic_data_upload.description: true sends the episodic diagnostic data.

eu_location.description: true keeps the diagnostic data in the EU data boundary.

sdn.description: SDN enabled by Azure Arc (Network Controller as a Failover Cluster service; Azure Local 2506 or later, OS build 26100 or later). It supports logical networks, network interfaces of Azure Local VMs and network security groups, and nothing else: no virtual networks, no software load balancer, no gateways. The older SDN managed by on-premises tools (SDN Express, Windows Admin Center, Network Controller VMs) is not built. https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/deploy/enable-sdn-integration

enabled.description: true to turn SDN enabled by Azure Arc on, which CANNOT BE UNDONE. Enable-ArcSdn.ps1 (phase 06, task 01) runs Add-EceFeature -Name NC on a machine of the instance when it is true. Microsoft Learn says that once SDN is enabled you cannot roll back or disable it, and false does not turn it off. Never set it where Network Controller was deployed with on-premises tools. Enabling interrupts the network of running workloads for a short time. New-NetworkSecurityGroup.ps1 (task 07) and New-LogicalNetwork.ps1 (task 08, for a logical network with nsg_name) also read it: network security groups need SDN enabled by Azure Arc.

prefix.description: The SDN prefix (Add-EceFeature -SDNPrefix). It names the Network Controller REST URL, https://<prefix>-NC.<domain>/, and tells the controllers of different instances apart. Microsoft Learn: not empty, eight characters or fewer, letters, digits and hyphens only, no two hyphens in a row, no hyphen at the end. The toolkit also refuses a hyphen at the start, which is not a valid DNS name. Required when sdn.enabled is true: Enable-ArcSdn.ps1 stops with exit 2 without it.

dns_records.description: How the A record <prefix>-NC of the Network Controller REST URL comes about. dynamic: Active Directory integrated dynamic DNS creates it when SDN is enabled and you do nothing. static: you create it first; it must resolve to the fifth address of networking.management.infrastructure_pool (Microsoft Learn: the fifth IP address of the range you gave at deployment) and to nothing else. Required when sdn.enabled is true. Enable-ArcSdn.ps1 resolves the name on the machine before it enables SDN and stops when the answer is wrong.

acknowledge_maintenance_window.description: true when you accept that enabling SDN interrupts the network of running workloads for a short time and that a maintenance window is arranged on a production instance (Add-EceFeature -AcknowledgeMaintenanceWindow). Enable-ArcSdn.ps1 asks nothing at run time, so this is the answer: it enables SDN only when this is true.

acknowledge_dns_record.description: true when the static DNS record <prefix>-NC exists and points at the fifth address of networking.management.infrastructure_pool (Add-EceFeature -AcknowledgeDNSRecordCreation). Read only when sdn.dns_records is static: with dynamic DNS Microsoft Learn asks for no acknowledgement.

operations.description: Day-2 choices: updates, backup, disaster recovery, notifications, licensing and monitoring. Only Azure Monitor (monitoring) and the notification addresses are read by the tools so far (the monitoring scripts of phase 02, operational foundations); the rest is not read yet. Sonar reads its own settings.

update_method.description: How updates are applied: portal or powershell. Documentation only; not read by the tools. operations.updates.install_after_deployment carries the part a script can act on.

updates.description: Schema 5.6.20. Updates after the deployment. Start-SolutionUpdateAfterDeployment.ps1 (scripts/lifecycle/updates/powershell) reads both keys. Learn: Update Azure Local by using PowerShell.

install_after_deployment.description: true: after the deployment, start the solution update (Start-SolutionUpdate) and return. The script does not wait: the update takes hours and the machines restart. false (default): no update is started. The script checks that the health of the update environment is not Failure, Error or Warning, and starts nothing when an update is already running or the instance is at the target. Sonar follows the run.

target_version.description: The solution version to install: latest (default; the highest solution update that is ready to install), or four numbers, for example 12.2610.1004.50, which the update service must list (Get-SolutionUpdate). Standalone Solution Builder Extension updates are not chosen.

backup.description: Backup of the instance and its workloads.

enabled.description: true when backup is part of the design.

approach.description: What is backed up: host, guest or both.

solution.description: Name of the backup solution, for example Azure Backup.

recovery_vault.description: Name of the Recovery Services vault. Not read by the tools yet: a documented placeholder.

resource_group.description: Resource group of the Recovery Services vault.

disaster_recovery.description: Disaster recovery of the workloads. Not read by the tools yet: a documented placeholder.

method.description: none, asr (Azure Site Recovery) or hyper_v_replica.

recovery_vault.description: Name of the Recovery Services vault used for replication. Not read by the tools yet: a documented placeholder.

resource_group.description: Resource group of the Recovery Services vault.

replication_policy.description: Name of the replication policy. Not read by the tools yet: a documented placeholder.

recovery_plan.description: Name of the recovery plan. Not read by the tools yet: a documented placeholder.

network.description: Network the VMs fail over to.

test_network.description: Isolated network for test failovers. Not read by the tools yet: a documented placeholder.

storage_account.description: Storage account that holds replication data.

target_rto_minutes.description: Recovery time objective in minutes. Not read by the tools yet: a documented placeholder.

target_rpo_minutes.description: Recovery point objective in minutes. Not read by the tools yet: a documented placeholder.

notifications.description: Who hears about alerts. Only email addresses: the action group of Azure Local alerting is an email group.

emails.description: Addresses (team mailboxes) that receive the notifications of the operations tools. Deploy-ActionGroup.ps1 makes each one an email receiver of the action group.

azure_hybrid_benefit.description: true to activate Azure Hybrid Benefit for Azure Local on the instance: it waives the Azure Local host service fee for an instance whose physical cores are covered by Windows Server Datacenter licenses with active Software Assurance. Enable-AzureHybridBenefit.ps1 (stage 05, phase 05, task 01) activates it with Invoke-AzStackHciExtendClusterSoftwareAssuranceBenefit. Activation cannot be undone, and Learn supports it only for hyperconverged instances with cloud connected management and no external storage, so the script refuses scenario.storage_architecture san or hybrid and scenario.connectivity disconnected. false or missing: the script does nothing; it never turns the benefit off.

windows_server_subscription.description: true when Windows Server guest licensing through Azure subscription is used. Not read by the tools yet: a documented placeholder.

azure_verification_for_vms.description: true when Azure Verification for VMs is turned on, so Windows Server 2025 guests get the Azure-only benefits. Not read by the tools yet: a documented placeholder.

monitoring.description: Azure Monitor for the instance. Only Azure Monitor (monitoring) and the notification addresses are read by the tools so far (the monitoring scripts of phase 02, operational foundations); the rest is not read yet. Sonar reads its own settings.

enabled.description: true when Azure Monitor is part of the design. When it is false, every monitoring script of phase 02 (workspace, endpoint, Azure Monitor Agent, Insights association, action group) does nothing and exits 0.

log_analytics_workspace.description: Name of the Log Analytics workspace. Deploy-LogAnalyticsWorkspace.ps1 creates it; Deploy-DataCollectionEndpoint.ps1 looks it up and takes the region of the endpoint from it. The Insights data collection rule sends to it.

workspace_resource_group.description: Resource group of the Log Analytics workspace. It is also the resource group of the data collection endpoint and of the action group that the monitoring scripts create and of the Insights data collection rule that Enable-HciInsights.ps1 looks up.

retention_days.description: How many days the workspace keeps its data (the default retention). Deploy-LogAnalyticsWorkspace.ps1 passes it when it creates the workspace; a workspace that exists is never changed. 30 is the Azure default and costs nothing extra; Microsoft Learn says retention beyond 31 days is charged. The pricing tier is not a key: a new workspace is pay-as-you-go, the commitment tiers start at 100 GB a day and the legacy tiers are closed to new customers.

data_collection_rule.description: Name of the existing data collection rule that Insights for Azure Local uses. Enable-HciInsights.ps1 (phase 02, task 03) looks it up in operations.monitoring.workspace_resource_group and associates it with the Arc machine of every node; it never creates or changes the rule. Microsoft Learn documents no template for the rule and says not to build your own, so create it once in the Azure portal (the instance, Capabilities, Insights, Get Started) and put its name here. Learn names the AzureStackHCI- prefix for the rule the portal creates.

data_collection_endpoint.description: Name of the data collection endpoint that Deploy-DataCollectionEndpoint.ps1 creates, in the region of the workspace.

action_group.description: Name of the Azure Monitor action group that tells the operations team about alerts. Deploy-ActionGroup.ps1 creates it, with an email receiver for each address of operations.notifications.emails and operations.monitoring.alert_email. Letters, digits, space and . _ - ( ), starting with a letter or digit.

alert_email.description: Address that receives the alerts (a team mailbox). Deploy-ActionGroup.ps1 makes it an email receiver of the action group, next to the addresses of operations.notifications.emails.

provisioning.description: How the OS gets onto the machines (scenario.os_install), and the OS version.

os_version.description: The solution version the machines run: latest, latest-preview, or a version such as 12.2610.1004.50. Pin a version. Simplified provisioning installs it, and the SBE must be validated with it.

iso.description: OS installed from an ISO. There is no unattended install: the OS is installed, then the tools take over.

image_source.description: microsoft (the Azure portal download) or oem (the OEM's image). Documentation only; not read by the tools. A record of where the ISO came from.

image_uri.description: Schema 5.6.19. Where each machine's BMC fetches the OS ISO from, as the address you give the virtual media of the BMC (Redfish VirtualMedia.InsertMedia): an http, https, nfs or cifs address of the ISO. Invoke-MountGoldImageISO.ps1 (phase 02, task 02) inserts it as the virtual CD of every machine in nodes[].

simplified.description: Simplified machine provisioning from Azure, as azurelocal-ztp runs it. https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-local/deploy/simplified-machine-provisioning

site_name.description: Resource name of the Microsoft.Edge site.

subscription_id.description: Subscription of the site and edge machines, when it isn't azure.subscription_id.

resource_group.description: Resource group of the site and edge machines, when it isn't azure.resource_group.

maintenance_iso.description: The provisioning (maintenance environment) ISO: latest, a train such as 2610, a build such as 10.2610.0.3063, or a Microsoft download URL.

admin.description: The local administrator that the provisioned OS gets. Prepare signs in as <node>\<username>.

username.description: Name of the local administrator the OS install creates on each machine (Learn: step 3, provision machines from Azure).

password.description: At least 12 characters with lowercase, uppercase, a digit and a special character. Create the secret before the run.

maintenance_password.description: Schema 5.3. The password of the maintenance environment's local user (edgeuser), which azurelocal-ztp's Device stage signs in with to reach the Configurator service before the machine is claimed. A Key Vault reference. Default: the maintenance environment's out-of-box password that Microsoft Learn documents (Configurator App article). Set a secret when the images carry another one.

media_share.description: The SMB share the BMCs mount the images from.

name.description: Name of the SMB share ZTP creates over the folder of the virtual USB images: letters, digits and hyphens.

host.description: The management host's address as the BMCs reach it.

host_adapter.description: Instead of host: the local adapter whose IPv4 address the BMCs reach. Wins over host.

account_name.description: Schema 5.4. The local account azurelocal-ztp creates on the management host to give the BMCs access to the share (it generates a password for it, and removes the account with the share). Default: svc-ztp-media.

keep.description: Schema 5.4. Keep the share, its firewall rule and the account after the vouchers are collected (azurelocal-ztp removes them by default). Default false.

media_path.description: Schema 5.2. Folder on the management host for the run's downloads and data: the maintenance ISO cache, the SBE copy and its unpacked drivers, the per-node USB images (about 4 GB each), the vouchers and the run state. Outside any git working tree: azurelocal-ztp refuses a folder inside one, and creates it when missing. Default: %ProgramData%\AzureLocalZtp\<site_name>\media.

evidence_path.description: Schema 5.2. Folder on the management host for the run's evidence: the event log monitors follow (ztp-events.jsonl), the BIOS and other Redfish change logs, and run logs. Outside any git working tree, created when missing. Default: %ProgramData%\AzureLocalZtp\<site_name>\evidence.

isolate_san_adapters.description: Schema 5.4. While the OS installs, turn off the PCIe slots that hold the SAN adapters listed in nodes[].san.hbas[], so the maintenance environment can't install onto a SAN LUN; put each back in the Restore stage to the value it had before the install (the vendor's enabled value if it was already disabled). azurelocal-ztp derives the BIOS attribute from the slot label and the vendor (config/oem/<vendor>.json, bios section). Default: true when any node lists san.hbas, false otherwise. An explicit hardware.bios or bios_during_provisioning key for the same attribute wins. A vendor without a slot mapping needs the raw attribute in bios_during_provisioning.

enable_embedded_nics.description: Schema 5.4. When a node's management or provisioning port has slot Embedded (an onboard LOM), make sure the embedded NICs are enabled in the BIOS (Dell ships them as DisabledOs, and the OS then can't see them): azurelocal-ztp sets the vendor's embedded-NIC attribute at the Boot stage and leaves it set. Default true. Does nothing when no such port is listed. An explicit hardware.bios key for the same attribute wins.

create_resource_group.description: Schema 5.4. Create the resource group of the site and edge machines (azure.resource_group, or provisioning.simplified.resource_group) when it does not exist. Default true. Set false when a landing zone creates resource groups and azurelocal-ztp should stop if it is missing.

configuration_name.description: Schema 5.4. Name of the Microsoft.Edge/configurations resource (the site configuration). Default: default.

managed_resource_group_name.description: Schema 5.4. Name for the managed resource group of the site configuration, which holds the Arc machines. Default: empty, the service chooses the name.

apply_site_settings.description: Schema 5.4. Create the site's network, time, connectivity and security settings (Microsoft.Edge/configurations child resources). Default true. Set false when the site configuration already carries them.

use_key_vault_configuration.description: Schema 5.4. Reference the Key Vault in the site's security settings, which the provisioning administrator secret needs. Default true.

assign_provisioning_roles.description: Schema 5.4. Give each edge machine its constrained role delegations on the resource group and on the Key Vault. Default true. Set false when your landing zone assigns them.

assign_hci_rp_role.description: Schema 5.4. Give the Azure Local resource provider its Azure Connected Machine Resource Manager role on the resource group. Default true. Set false when the resource group already has this assignment under another name (the deployment would fail with RoleAssignmentExists).

network_kind.description: Schema 5.4. Kind of the site's network setting: LAN or WLAN. Default LAN.

ntp.description: Schema 5.4. The time setting of the site configuration, used while the machines are provisioned. Default: Automatic. (networking.ntp_servers is OS configuration; it is not copied here.)

server.description: The NTP server (address or name) when configuration is Manual.

alternate_server.description: The alternate NTP server when configuration is Manual.

site_mode.description: Schema 5.4. Auto (create the site and configuration when missing), Create (they must not exist) or Reuse (they must exist). Default Auto.

deployment_name.description: Schema 5.4. Name of the ARM deployment. Default: ztp-<site_name>.

skip_azure_check.description: Schema 5.4. Skip the Bootstrap stage's check of the Azure prerequisites (the feature, the resource providers and the catalog). Default false.

include_preview.description: Schema 5.4. Resolve stage: also consider preview trains when maintenance_iso is latest. Default false.

max_train.description: Schema 5.4. Resolve stage: the highest train to consider when maintenance_iso is latest, for example 2609 to stay on the train of a given solution release. Default: none.

retry_provision_os.description: Schema 5.4. Resubmit a failed OS install job once. Default true.

usb_image.description: Schema 5.4. The per-node virtual USB image that carries the maintenance ISO.

size_gb.description: Image size in GiB. The maintenance ISO needs about 1 GiB; 4 is the size that booted on Dell 16G servers. Default 4.

name_prefix.description: File-name prefix of the images (<prefix><node>.img). Default ztp-usb-.

maintenance_environment.description: Schema 5.4. The maintenance environment's Configurator service, which the Device stage reaches before the claim.

port.description: TCP port of the service (https://<address>:<port>/BootstrapOobeService). Default 20001, the port Microsoft documents.

username.description: The service's local user. Default edgeuser, as Microsoft documents. Its password is maintenance_password.

timeouts.description: Schema 5.4. How long azurelocal-ztp waits at each stage, and how often it polls. The defaults are the values that worked on Dell AX servers; a server with a long POST (large memory) or a slow link may need more.

bootstrap_minutes.description: Bootstrap stage: overall budget until the maintenance environment is up and every node is ready for the portal. Default 120.

bootstrap_voucher_minutes.description: Bootstrap stage: budget until a valid voucher appears. Default 90.

bootstrap_stall_minutes.description: Bootstrap stage: how long the BMC may show no change before the stage reports a stall. Default 20.

voucher_wait_minutes.description: Vouchers stage: how long to wait for each node's voucher in its image. Default 120.

device_minutes.description: Device stage: how long the maintenance environment may take to report the static address (and to be found by the scan). Default 30.

ready_minutes.description: Ready stage: polling budget until every machine is ready to cluster. Default 180.

network_minutes.description: Network stage: how long each Azure configuration job may take. Default 60.

restore_settle_minutes.description: Restore stage: how long to wait after the BIOS restart before checking that the Arc machines are Connected again. Default 5.

bios_minutes.description: Boot and Restore stages: how long to wait for a node's BIOS to report the new values after the restart. Default 30.

adapters_minutes.description: Network stage: how long to wait for an edge machine to report its network adapters. The stage polls every poll_interval_seconds (at least 5) until the management MAC is in the list, because the list can still be empty right after Ready. Default 10; 0 reads once and does not wait. When the budget is spent without the management MAC the machine is not verified in any mode (adapters never reported, a Warning that is never a success state) and the Handoff stage reads the adapters again.

poll_interval_seconds.description: Ready and Network stages: seconds between polls. Default 60.

os_configuration.description: How the toolkit's OS configuration run (Invoke-AzureLocalOsConfiguration.ps1) treats the machines after the OS is installed, whichever way it was installed. Optional; every key has a default. (since 5.4.3)

clear_storage.description: Wipe the leftover local storage (storage pools, virtual disks and the data on non-boot, non-system local disks) of every machine in the OS configuration run's Apply mode, so a re-used machine starts clean. Boot, system, SAN (Fibre Channel, iSCSI) and USB disks are never touched. The Plan mode lists the disks per machine and wipes nothing; in a pipeline that list is what the approval gate shows. Default false: leftover storage is reported as blocking, and nothing is wiped. (since 5.4.3)

network.description: How a guarded network change is confirmed (since 5.4.4): the management address, gateway, DNS, VLAN, the remote-management firewall rules, DHCP off on the other ports and disabled adapters are staged on the node, which applies and checks them and reverts by itself unless the orchestrator confirms through a new session on the new address.

confirm_minutes.description: The window for the orchestrator's confirmation. With no confirmation inside it the node restores its snapshot. The run setting networkRollbackMinutes overrides it. (since 5.4.4)

stable_seconds.description: How long the node's own checks must stay green before it waits for the confirmation. The run setting networkStableSeconds overrides it. (since 5.4.4)

remoting.description: How the OS configuration reaches the nodes and how their remote management (WinRM, RDP, ICMP) is secured. The environment class (scenario.environment_class) picks the profile; these keys refine it. The baseline holds in every class and no key changes it: AllowUnencrypted false, Basic and CredSSP off, no SkipCACheck or SkipCNCheck, TLS 1.2 or higher. transport, bootstrap_transport and allowed_source_cidrs are since 5.4.4; the other keys are since 5.6.

transport.description: winrm (HTTP, 5985), winrm_https (5986, a certificate on the node) or arc (Azure Arc Run Command: the exception for sites with no route to the nodes; not recommended for network changes). The command line's -Transport WinRM or ArcRunCommand overrides it.

bootstrap_transport.description: How a node whose WinRM firewall rule blocks this host is opened once, without touching the node by hand. none: such a node fails with the diagnosis. arc: Azure Arc Run Command (outbound 443 only; the wait is capped, default 3 minutes, then the route fails cleanly). smb: TCP 445 from a Windows orchestrator to the node, the local Administrator, one small service run once with sc.exe; Windows orchestrator only. auto: the allowed routes in the order smb, arc. Each runs one small script that starts WinRM, creates the listener if none exists and sets the WinRM rules' scope, then everything else runs over WinRM. production and dmz also need the pipeline approval (-ApprovedBootstrap). The environment class decides whether a bootstrap is allowed at all.

allowed_source_cidrs.description: The runner and jump server addresses, as the node sees them (after NAT), allowed to use WinRM, RDP and ICMP on the nodes, in addition to the management and out-of-band networks. IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR; /0 to /8 is refused, dev and production refuse anything wider than /24 (/64 for IPv6), dmz takes /32 or /128 only. The dmz class does not add the management network.

allow_any_source.description: true: the nodes' firewall accepts WinRM, RDP and ICMP from any source (and TrustedHosts is '*' on the machine running the automation). Honoured only in the classes lab and test, where it is implied unless you set false; it is an error in dev, production and dmz.

trusted_hosts.description: The TrustedHosts policy on the machine running the automation. auto: the class decides. exact: only the nodes' addresses. wildcard: '*', lab and test only. The previous value is restored after the run.

use_https.description: auto: the class decides (HTTP in lab and test; HTTPS in dev, production and dmz). true: WinRM over HTTPS (5986). false: HTTP only, which production and dmz refuse and dev warns about.

isolation_confirmed.description: true: you confirm the network of the nodes has no route to production. Only a statement in lab and test (it changes the warning text, not the behaviour); it is not allowed in dev, production or dmz, where Any is never accepted.

certificate.description: The server certificate for the HTTPS listener: the 40-hex thumbprint of a certificate already in the node's LocalMachine\My store, or keyvault://<vault>/<secret> of a secret that holds the certificate as a base64 PFX without a password (a Key Vault certificate's secret). Empty: each node gets a self-signed Server Authentication certificate with its DNS names and management IP as subject alternative names, as the pre-join bootstrap only (not allowed in dmz).

Optional.

A subnet names its group in landing_zone.networks[].subnets[].network_security_group; New-LandingZoneNsg.ps1 (phase 04, manual deployment, task 06) creates each group listed here in the subscription, resource group and region of every network whose subnets name it (Deploy-VirtualNetworks.ps1 looks the group up there and attaches it), and adds the rules that are missing. rules.description: Schema 5.6.21. The security rules of the group. A group with no rules has only the default rules Azure adds (Microsoft Learn, Azure network security groups overview). The script adds the rules that are missing; a rule that exists with the same name is left alone and, when it differs from the file, reported. It never removes or changes a rule.

name.description: Schema 5.6.21. Name of the rule, 1 to 80 characters, with the same characters as the group name. Unique inside the group.

access.description: Schema 5.6.21. Allow or Deny the traffic the rule matches.

node.description: One machine. Describe its management port either with management (schema 5.0) or, from 5.2, with network_adapters, which lists every port and derives management from the port that owns the management address.

name.description: Host name: up to 15 characters. Also the edge machine name and, for an ISO install, the Arc machine name. With simplified provisioning the Arc machine name is arc_machine_name, which defaults to this.

management.description: The machine's management port and address (schema 5.0 and 5.1). From 5.2, network_adapters describes it instead: the port with role management and an ip_assignment other than none. When both are given they must agree; prefer network_adapters.

ip_address.description: Management address. ARM physicalNodesSettings[].ipv4Address. How it gets onto the management port before deployment is networking.management.ip_assignment: set on the port (static), reserved in DHCP for mac_address (dhcp), or already there (preconfigured). With network_adapters it is the management port's ip_address.

mac_address.description: MAC of the management port. Provisioning finds and targets the port by it: simplified provisioning names the port by this MAC when it sets the static address (edge machine networkAdapters[].macAddress), and node preparation finds the adapter by it. With ip_assignment dhcp, reserve ip_address for this MAC. Required with simplified provisioning.

adapter_name.description: Name of the management port in the installed OS, for example 'SLOT 3 Port 1'. Optional: mac_address identifies the port. Simplified provisioning also sends it with the port's settings; leave it out unless you know the name the OS gives the port.

network_adapters.description: Every physical network port of the machine (schema 5.2): name, MAC, roles and how each gets its host address. Exactly one port owns the management address: role management and an ip_assignment other than none. Intents name ports by these names. List them on every node or on none.

serial_number.description: Serial number (Dell service tag). Maps each simplified-provisioning voucher to its machine.

zone.description: Rack-aware: the local availability zone. ARM localAvailabilityZones.

storage_ips.description: Storage address on each storage network, in networking.storage.networks order, when networking.storage.auto_ip is false.

arc_machine_name.description: Name of the machine's Arc resource (Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines). Default: name. Simplified provisioning sets it when it claims the machine (edge machine arcMachineResourceId); without it the service names the Arc machine ROE1-<id>, and an Arc machine can't be renamed. The deployment uses it in ARM arcNodeResourceIds. An ISO install registers the Arc machine under the host name, so leave it out there. 1-54 letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.', not ending in '.'.

arc_resource_name.description: Deprecated: use arc_machine_name. Read as arc_machine_name when that isn't set.

bios.description: BIOS attributes for this machine in their FINAL state, merged over hardware.bios (a key here wins). See hardware.bios.

bios_during_provisioning.description: Schema 5.3. Temporary BIOS attributes for this machine's OS install only, merged over hardware.bios_during_provisioning (a key here wins); during-provisioning values win over bios. azurelocal-ztp sets each key back to its bios value in its Restore stage. See hardware.bios_during_provisioning.

maintenance_address.description: Schema 5.3. Simplified provisioning: the address the machine's maintenance environment answers on (its Configurator service, TCP 20001), when it is known: a DHCP reservation, or an address set at the console. azurelocal-ztp's Device stage then talks to it directly. Without it, the Device stage finds the maintenance environment by MAC, scanning networking.management.provisioning_dhcp_range.

san.description: Schema 5.3. This machine's SAN connections: its Fibre Channel HBAs and their WWPNs (storage.san.type fibre_channel), or its iSCSI initiator IQN (storage.san.type iscsi; the iSCSI ports' addresses are on network_adapters with role iscsi:a and iscsi:b). Needed on every machine when storage.san.type is set.

adapters.description: Adapters of the intent, by the key nodes[].network_adapters[].name (the port's name in this file, the same on every machine; the file finds the physical adapter by its MAC, so the OS may call it anything). With nodes[].network_adapters (5.2) each name must be a port in every node's list. The name the deployment sends to Azure (ARM intentList adapter) is what the OS calls that adapter on the nodes, found by MAC, or nodes[].network_adapters[].os_name_override when the file sets one. The first adapter matters: the management virtual adapter takes the MAC of the first adapter of the management intent, so that adapter owns the management address.

overrides.description: Network ATC overrides. Leave out to keep Network ATC's defaults, which Microsoft recommends.

purpose.description: What the network is for (since 5.6). management and oob mark a network the machines' remote management may be reached from: the remote management security profile adds its subnet to the allowed sources of dev and production (a candidate, not a trust: prefer listing the controller addresses in os_configuration.remoting.allowed_source_cidrs). automation, compute, storage and other have no effect on remote management.

bios_settings.description: BIOS attributes: vendor attribute name -> value, as the BMC's Redfish Bios resource names them (Attributes of /redfish/v1/Systems/<id>/Bios). Values are strings, even for numbers; tools convert them to the type the BMC reports. azurelocal-ztp applies them in its Boot stage, before the maintenance boot: it reads the current values, PATCHes only those that differ to the Bios Settings resource with @Redfish.SettingsApplyTime OnReset, powers the machine on or restarts it, and waits until the BIOS reports every value. Used twice: as bios (the machine's FINAL state) and as bios_during_provisioning (TEMPORARY values for the OS install, which the Restore stage sets back to the bios values). Dell examples: Slot2: Disabled (turn off the card in PCIe slot 2, for example a Fibre Channel HBA whose SAN LUN the maintenance environment would otherwise install onto; as a temporary value, with Slot2: Enabled in bios); Slot2: BootDriverDisabled (the card stays visible to the OS but never boots); EmbNic1Nic2: Enabled (the embedded LOM ports, when they show as DisabledOs and the OS can't see them).

additionalProperties.description: The value of the BIOS attribute, as a string.

wwpn.description: A Fibre Channel World Wide Port Name: 16 hexadecimal digits, as 8 colon-separated pairs (50:00:09:72:08:12:34:56) or without colons.

iscsi_name.description: An iSCSI qualified name (iqn.yyyy-mm.reversed.domain[:identifier]), or an eui. or naa. name.

iscsi_portal.description: An iSCSI target portal: an IPv4 address, optionally with :port (default 3260).

node_san.description: One machine's SAN connections (schema 5.3). Fibre Channel: hbas, each with its slot and ports, and every port's WWPN and fabric. iSCSI: initiator_iqn.

hbas.description: The host bus adapters in this machine that reach the SAN: Fibre Channel HBAs, and from 5.4 iSCSI offload adapters. azurelocal-ztp reads their slots (schema 5.4): while the OS installs it turns those PCIe slots off in the BIOS, so the maintenance environment can't install onto a SAN LUN, and turns them on again afterwards (provisioning.simplified.isolate_san_adapters).

slot.description: Where the HBA is, as a PCIe slot label: Slot 2, Slot2 or slot-2 (the number is what counts). azurelocal-ztp turns the BIOS attribute of that slot off for the OS install and puts it back afterwards; the attribute name per vendor is in its config/oem/<vendor>.json. For another label (for example OCP 1), or a vendor azurelocal-ztp has no mapping for, give bios_attribute.

type.description: Schema 5.4. fibre_channel (default; with storage.san.type fibre_channel the ports with their WWPNs are needed for zoning, rule AZL-028) or iscsi_offload (an adapter that presents SAN LUNs to the BIOS; it needs no ports here, its addresses are on network_adapters with role iscsi:a or iscsi:b).

bios_attribute.description: Schema 5.4. The vendor's BIOS attribute name for this adapter's slot, as the BMC's Redfish Bios resource names it. With no vendor mapping in azurelocal-ztp this is the only way to isolate the adapter during the install; with a mapping it overrides the attribute derived from slot. An explicit bios_during_provisioning key for the same attribute still wins.

bios_disabled_value.description: Schema 5.4. The value of bios_attribute that turns the slot off for the OS install. Default: the vendor mapping's disabled value, else Disabled.

bios_enabled_value.description: Schema 5.4. The value that turns the slot back on when azurelocal-ztp finds it already at bios_disabled_value in the Restore stage (for example a crashed earlier run left it off). Otherwise Restore puts back the value it found before the install. Default: the vendor mapping's enabled value, else Enabled.

initiator_iqn.description: The machine's iSCSI initiator name. Unique in the file.

network_adapter.description: One physical network port of the machine (schema 5.2). List every port, used or not, so each tool reads the same NICs. A port can carry several roles (a converged design).

name.description: The port's name in this file: the key that networking.intents[].adapters, networking.storage.networks[].adapter and networking.cluster_networks[].adapter use. The same on every machine, unique on the machine. It labels a physical adapter that is found on the node by mac_address, so it does not have to be the name the OS gave the adapter (OS names differ between installs and between ZTP and ISO installs, for example Port0, SLOT 3 Port 1 or NIC1). Discovery writes it from the slot and the port, for example 'Slot 3 Port 1'. The name the deployment sends to Azure is what the OS calls the adapter (read by MAC) or os_name_override when set. A file that already uses the OS name here keeps working.

mac_address.description: The port's identity. Tools find the physical adapter on a node by this MAC (case and separators are ignored), never by a name: node preparation, the ARM parameters and the pre-cluster verification all resolve the OS adapter name from it. Hardware discovery writes it. Required. Also needed for a DHCP reservation and, with simplified provisioning, for the management port.

slot.description: Where the port is, for example Embedded (a LOM), Slot 3 or OCP 1. From 5.4 azurelocal-ztp reads it: a management or provisioning port in slot Embedded makes it enable the embedded NICs in the BIOS (provisioning.simplified.enable_embedded_nics), and a slot that also holds a SAN adapter (nodes[].san.hbas[].slot) is never turned off.

port_index.description: The number of the port on its adapter, counted from 1, as the BMC reports it (Redfish PhysicalPortNumber, else the order of the port on the card). With slot and pci_location it says which physical connector the port is. Written by hardware discovery; a record of the hardware, nothing is configured from it.

pci_location.description: Where the adapter sits on the PCI bus, as hardware discovery reports it (bus, device, function as decimal numbers). A verification aid, informational: OS configuration compares it with the node's own hardware information (Get-NetAdapterHardwareInfo) and reports a difference; the port is still found by mac_address.

vendor.description: The adapter manufacturer as hardware discovery reports it, for example the Manufacturer of the Redfish NetworkAdapter. Informational: no tool behaves differently for a brand; every make is handled through the same keys (mac_address, slot, port_index, model, speed_gbps, rdma).

os_name_override.description: Optional, off by default. The name you want this adapter to have in the OS, for example 'Mgmt1', 'Compute1' or 'Storage1'. Without it nothing is renamed: the OS configuration step NicNames leaves every adapter name alone and the deployment sends the name the OS already uses (found by mac_address). With it, NicNames renames the adapter found by mac_address to this name (a guarded change, idempotent, the management adapter last) and the deployment sends this name. Give the same value for the same port (name) on every machine: Network ATC needs one adapter name per intent adapter on every node. 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, space, underscore, dot, hyphen and parentheses.

model.description: Card model, for example 'NVIDIA ConnectX-6 Dx'. Ports in one intent must be the same make, model and speed.

roles.description: What the port is for: management, compute, storage (the Network ATC traffic types), provisioning (the maintenance environment of simplified provisioning reaches Azure through this port, before the machine is claimed; how it gets its address there is networking.management.provisioning_network), iscsi:a or iscsi:b (schema 5.3: a port that carries iSCSI traffic to the SAN's fabric A or B; give it a static address, prefix_length and VLAN, no gateway), or unused. A converged port lists several, for example [management, compute]. unused stands alone.

ip_assignment.description: How the installed OS gets this port's host address before deployment. For the management port this is the management address mode (config/variables/docs/infrastructure-file.md): dhcp_reservation is Mode A (Reserved, recommended); static is Mode B (Static with DHCP) or Mode C (Static without management DHCP). static: ip_address is set on the port (with simplified provisioning azurelocal-ztp's Device stage sets it by MAC before the OS install, the install resets every port to DHCP, and OS configuration sets it again by MAC; otherwise the operator or the toolkit). dhcp_reservation: the port keeps DHCP and the DHCP server reserves ip_address for mac_address. dhcp: the port keeps DHCP with no reservation, so its address can change (a warning). preconfigured: the port is already configured; tools leave it alone. none: no host address before deployment (Network ATC or the storage networks give it one, or it isn't used); node preparation turns DHCP off on it. Exactly one management port per machine owns the management address: the one with role management and an ip_assignment other than none.

ip_address.description: The host address. For the management port this is ARM physicalNodesSettings[].ipv4Address. Required with static. With dhcp_reservation give the reserved address: without it the tools can only check that the port has a DHCP address (a warning), and the deployment still needs it unless use_dhcp is true (a file with scope ztp doesn't deploy).

prefix_length.description: Prefix length of ip_address. Default for the management port: from networking.management.subnet, which it must match.

gateway.description: Default gateway on this port. Default for the management port: networking.management.gateway. Leave it out on every other port: validation fails when more than one physical adapter has a default gateway.

dns_servers.description: Default for the management port: networking.management.dns_servers, which it must match.

vlan_id.description: The VLAN of this port's traffic. With vlan_mode tagged the host tags it; with vlan_mode access the switch port is an access port in this VLAN and the host sends untagged frames (it records the switch side). Without vlan_mode, 0 or absent means untagged and anything else is tagged by the host.

vlan_mode.description: access: the switch port is an access (untagged) port; the host doesn't tag, so simplified provisioning sends VLAN 0. tagged: the switch port is a trunk and the host tags vlan_id.

allowed_vlans.description: Optional. The VLAN ids the switch port of this adapter allows, when the port is a trunk that carries more than the VLAN of the port itself: the tenant (compute) VLANs of the compute adapters. The pre-cluster verification checks that every VLAN used by compute traffic in networking.vlans[] and networking.logical_networks[] is in this list on the compute adapters; without it a tagged compute port is reported Skipped (the file says nothing about what the port allows). This is switch-side metadata for the checklist of the gate; it does not configure the switch or the NIC.

switch.description: The switch, for example a network_devices[].hostname.

port.description: The switch port, for example Ethernet1/11.

allOf.description: Schema 5.3, _metadata.scope. ztp: only what azurelocal-ztp reads is required. full (default): the whole instance, as in 5.0 to 5.2.

sbe.description: hardware.sbe is optional in a file with scope ztp. When it is there, ZTP prepares the machines from its bundle_path, or the file states requirement (required or not_applicable).

When hardware.sbe is present it names the package: bundle_path or source_path (the identity is read from the package), or publisher, family and version for an SBE you placed in C:\SBE yourself, or requirement not_applicable (with not_applicable_reason). Without hardware.sbe the vendor catalog decides whether a package is required (the pre-cluster verification, SB-001). Nothing here adds a default that turns a build-time side-load on.

management.description: The infrastructure pool is a cluster-deployment setting, so a file with scope ztp doesn't need it. It is required unless use_dhcp is true.
